Finish active agent/terminal/background work before upgrading. The installer verifies and stops only its own idle Hub, stages the payload and rolls back touched application files on an error. Logs are under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ChatMCP\logs`. A retained `.chatmcp-update-pending.json` indicates an interrupted update or a rollback that could not put every file back; keep its backup directory rather than deleting it or launching a mixed bundle, and see "Repairing an installation that an update left halfway" below.

Setup names what it puts in front of a person DatGold Studio: the Desktop shortcut, the Start menu folder `DatGold` (the launcher and the uninstaller) and the entry in Windows Settings > Apps > Installed apps. Versions up to 3.10.1 used the old product name for these. When setup installs over such a version it removes those shortcuts (only the ones that point into the installation it is replacing, whichever shortcut choices the wizard shows) and their Start menu folder if nothing else is in it; the uninstaller removes both sets. A tile pinned to the taskbar or to Start from an old shortcut keeps its old name until it is unpinned and pinned again. Which names keep the old spelling, and why: [naming](NAMING.md).

Unattended installation is opt-in and has the same safety checks as the wizard:

~~~powershell
# The setup of releases up to v3.10.2 is called ChatMCPSetup.exe.
.\DatGoldSetup.exe --quiet --install-dir "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\ChatMCP"
# Use only from the actual installed directory:
.\Uninstall.exe --quiet --uninstall
# An installation that an update left halfway (see "Repairing an installation that an update left halfway"):
.\DatGoldSetup.exe --quiet --recover --install-dir "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\ChatMCP"
~~~

Exit 1 indicates failure. Installing the desktop does not silently replace a Browser Companion loaded unpacked from another directory; update/reload that extension separately.

**Update mode.** The desktop app starts the setup of a downloaded release in a third form, after it has checked the file itself (`docs/THREAT-MODEL.md`, Surface 8): `DatGoldSetup.exe --quiet --update --install-dir "<the installation>" [--wait-pid <process id>] [--relaunch] [--result "<drive>:\...\x.json"]`. The two quiet forms above take exactly the arguments they took before; an update takes exactly these, each at most once, and anything else is refused with the usage text. With `--wait-pid` the setup waits at most 30 seconds for that process to exit, and only when it is the installed `ChatMCP.exe`; a process id that is gone, or has been handed on to another program, is not waited for. `--relaunch` opens the right app at the end: the new one after an update, the old one after a refusal or a clean rollback, and none while `.chatmcp-update-pending.json` is on disk (the launcher would refuse to start). `--result` names a `.json` file on a drive, which the setup writes whole, as one line: `{"format":1,"ok":true,"version":"x.y.z","previous":"x.y.z","state":"installed","reason":null,"rolledBack":false}` where `state` is `installed`, `unchanged` (nothing was replaced), `rolled_back` (files were replaced and all of them put back) and `needs_recovery` (the rollback is incomplete, or an earlier update left its marker: the marker and the backup stay and the launcher, the setup's install form and the uninstaller refuse to go on until the installation is repaired, see below; when the setup repaired it, the file says `rolled_back` instead, with the reason the update failed for), and `reason` is one of `shell_not_exited`, `no_installation`, `not_newer`, `disk_full`, `pending_recovery`, `tasks_running`, `foreign_listener`, `hub_stop_failed`, `window_open`, `another_update`, `payload_invalid`, `install_failed` (never the text of an exception, which can hold a path). The app gives it a path in the Hub's data folder (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\ChatMCP\hub\update-result.json`); the setup writes the file only when no program listens on port 3007, because the Hub reads it once, when it starts, and removes it (a note left beside a Hub that is already running would be read by nobody until some later start). A refusal that stopped nothing, such as a task that is running, is told in the window of the update and leaves no file. When the rollback of this update could not put every file back, the setup waits 3 seconds and repairs the installation itself, once (see below); the file is then written after that, with the state `rolled_back`. The setup says in its window that the app was opened again only when it really was. This form never reinstalls or downgrades (`not_newer`), refuses an earlier update that did not finish (`pending_recovery`) and a disk with less room than the payload plus 128 MiB or a quarter of it (`disk_full`), keeps the shortcuts the installation has (a shortcut that was deleted stays deleted; the ones that versions up to 3.10.1 made under the old product name are replaced by the DatGold ones) and applies the same checks for work and for a foreign listener as the other forms. While it works it shows a small window with no button; after a failure the window says why, in what state DatGold is left, and has one button, Close, and, when the installation needs repair and has not been repaired, a second one, Repair now (which takes both away while it works). Exit code 0 means that the new version is in place.

**Repairing an installation that an update left halfway.** When an update stops halfway and its rollback cannot put every file back (a file was in use, or the setup was killed, or the power went), the file `.chatmcp-update-pending.json` stays in the installation folder together with a backup folder it names (`.ChatMCP-update-<id>`, holding `journal.json` and the files that were replaced). DatGold does not start behind it (the launcher says what to run), and the setup's install form and the uninstaller refuse to go on. The setup puts the installation back itself from that backup:

- **In the window of the update.** When the rollback of this very update left the marker, the setup waits 3 seconds and repairs the installation once, by itself, and says so. This happens only when the install itself failed: after a refusal that came before it (another setup working on the folder, a task that runs) the setup repairs nothing by itself. If it was refused, or when the marker is an earlier update's or was left by something else, the window has a button, **Repair now**, which does it (again); it tells you why when it cannot, and you can press it again once the cause is gone, for instance a program that holds a file open.
- **With the setup wizard.** Run `DatGoldSetup.exe`: when the folder you install into holds the marker, the wizard asks whether to repair it first and then installs.
- **With the repair form.** `DatGoldSetup.exe --quiet --recover --install-dir "<the DatGold folder>"` repairs the installation and nothing else. The setup is a Windows program with no console of its own, so a prompt that is just given the command shows nothing and does not wait: run it so that the shell waits and shows the line, for instance `.\DatGoldSetup.exe --quiet --recover --install-dir "<the DatGold folder>" 2>&1 | Out-Host; $LASTEXITCODE` in Windows PowerShell. It prints one line and exits 0 when the installation is whole (repaired, or there was nothing to repair) and 1 for everything else: the repair was refused (nothing was changed), it stopped halfway (run it again), a task runs or another update works on the folder, the folder is not there, or the arguments are wrong. It must be run from a DatGoldSetup.exe that is not in the DatGold folder; it takes no other argument.

The repair puts a file back only when it is the bytes the update wrote or the old ones, and removes a file the update created only when it is the bytes the update wrote. **It refuses, and changes nothing,** when it cannot prove that the installation is what the journal says: the backup is missing or damaged, `journal.json` cannot be read (setups up to 3.10.2 did not flush it to the disk), a file was changed by something else after the update began, or a name leads outside the installation or through a link. Nothing is put back outside the DatGold folder, and a name in the data folder of the Hub is refused; the only other things written are the repair's own log (in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ChatMCP\logs`, also when it refuses) and, in the window of an update, the result file. A stop in the middle (the power goes again, a file is held open) is repaired by running it again. After a repair made by the window of an update, the next start of DatGold says that the update did not go through (only that window writes the result file, and only when no program listens on port 3007: a repair made by the wizard or by `--recover`, or after a setup that was killed, leaves none, and DatGold then says nothing); a Hub that you start by hand, with `DATGOLD-HUB\START-CHATMCP-HUB.cmd` or `node hub.mjs`, leaves it alone while the marker is there, so it says nothing early. The repair was built for a rollback that could not finish and for a stop in the middle; it was run on what a commit killed in the middle leaves and by the lifecycle script on a disposable machine, and **not** after a real power cut or a real failed update.

**Recovering an installation by hand.** What can still be done when the repair above refuses because a file is neither what the update wrote nor what it replaced (somebody changed it, or an update that was cut off left it unfinished), and the only way for an older setup. It puts the installation back to what it was before the update whatever the files hold now, so read what it does first. Close DatGold, then run this in Windows PowerShell as the same user (set `$install` to the folder DatGold is installed in). It first checks that the journal lists something and that every backup is the file it was made from (the SHA-256 in the journal), and stops, changing nothing, when one is not: with a damaged backup there is nothing to put back from. Then it puts back every file the update replaced or removed from the backup folder of this installation, removes every file that the journal lists as created by the update, and removes the marker and the backup, so that DatGold and the setup work again:

~~~powershell
# recovery-from-retained-backup
$install = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\ChatMCP"
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$markerFile = Join-Path $install '.chatmcp-update-pending.json'
$named = ((Get-Content -LiteralPath $markerFile -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).backupDirectory).TrimEnd('\', '/')
$backups = Join-Path $install (Split-Path -Leaf $named)
$journal = Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $backups 'journal.json') -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
if (-not $journal) { throw 'The journal lists nothing. Nothing was changed.' }
foreach ($entry in $journal) {
    if ($entry.Backup) {
        $copy = Join-Path (Join-Path $backups 'old') (Split-Path -Leaf $entry.Backup)
        if ((Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $copy -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne $entry.OldHash) { throw "A backup is not the file it was made from: $($entry.Relative). Nothing was changed." }
    }
}
foreach ($entry in $journal) {
    $target = Join-Path $install ($entry.Relative -replace '/', '\')
    if ($entry.Backup) {
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Split-Path -Parent $target) | Out-Null
        Copy-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path (Join-Path $backups 'old') (Split-Path -Leaf $entry.Backup)) -Destination $target -Force
    } elseif (-not $entry.OldHash -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $target)) {
        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $target -Force
    }
}
Remove-Item -LiteralPath $markerFile -Force
Remove-Item -LiteralPath $backups -Recurse -Force
~~~

It stops at the first error. Up to the line that removes the marker nothing has been taken away, so it can be run again once the cause (a file that is open, say) is gone; after that line DatGold and the setup work again, and if the last line cannot remove the backup folder, that folder only takes up disk space and can be deleted by hand. It puts back what the journal lists: a file named like `<name>.<32 hexadecimal digits>.tmp` that a power cut left beside a file that was being replaced is not in the journal, and can be deleted by hand. The block is run for real on a retained backup by the native tests (`scripts/tests/native-lifecycle`), from this text, and by the lifecycle script (`scripts/tests/Test-NativeLifecycle.ps1`) on a disposable machine, which first checks that the real setup refuses to install behind the marker and refuses to repair a state in which a file was changed by something else, and then that the installation is whole again once the block has run. The repair of this section is run there too: in the real window of the update (the result file that it leaves and the old app that it opens again) and with the explicit form (twice).

To test the updater, build two versions that trust a key made for the run: `.\scripts\Build-Installer.ps1 -ReleaseKeysFile <full path of a key file>` builds that key list into the desktop shell and copies it over `CHATMCP-HUB\lib\release-keys.json` of the payload, so that the Hub the setup installs trusts the same list. The committed file is not touched, the script says that it is a test build, a publish workflow refuses the parameter, and the file must be a plain file of at most 16 KiB with an entry that says use `release` and a 91-byte key. The CI job "Windows in-app updater, end to end" does this for real on a hosted runner (`scripts/tests/updater-e2e/`): `Build-TestPair.ps1` builds an old and a newer setup of the commit under test side by side, with the versions given at build time and a key list that `scripts/new-release-key.mjs` made for the run, and `run.mjs` installs the old one, drives the page of the installed app with presses of the mouse that the browser takes for a person's (trusted clicks injected through the DevTools protocol, not the operating system's mouse), and lets the app update itself to the new one (a version is a plain `x.y.z`: the feed carries releases only, so a suffix such as `-test` is refused by the Hub and by the shell).

The installer and the uninstaller start Windows PowerShell as a child in two places: the helper that deletes `Uninstall.exe` once the uninstaller has ended, and the Hub ownership check of the preflight. A refusal that stopped nothing, such as a task that is running, is told in the window of the update and leaves no file. When the rollback of this update could not put every file back, the setup waits 3 seconds and repairs the installation itself, once (see below); the file is then written after that, with the state `rolled_back`. The setup says in its window that the app was opened again only when it really was. This form never reinstalls or downgrades (`not_newer`), refuses an earlier update that did not finish (`pending_recovery`) and a disk with less room than the payload plus 128 MiB or a quarter of it (`disk_full`), keeps the shortcuts the installation has (a shortcut that was deleted stays deleted; the ones that versions up to 3.10.1 made under the old product name are replaced by the DatGold ones) and applies the same checks for work and for a foreign listener as the other forms. While it works it shows a small window with no button; after a failure the window says why, in what state DatGold is left, and has one button, Close, and, when the installation needs repair and has not been repaired, a second one, Repair now (which takes both away while it works). Exit code 0 means that the new version is in place.

**Repairing an installation that an update left halfway.** When an update stops halfway and its rollback cannot put every file back (a file was in use, or the setup was killed, or the power went), the file `.chatmcp-update-pending.json` stays in the installation folder together with a backup folder it names (`.ChatMCP-update-<id>`, holding `journal.json` and the files that were replaced). DatGold does not start behind it (the launcher says what to run), and the setup's install form and the uninstaller refuse to go on. The setup puts the installation back itself from that backup:

- **In the window of the update.** When the rollback of this very update left the marker, the setup waits 3 seconds and repairs the installation once, by itself, and says so. This happens only when the install itself failed: after a refusal that came before it (another setup working on the folder, a task that runs) the setup repairs nothing by itself. If it was refused, or when the marker is an earlier update's or was left by something else, the window has a button, **Repair now**, which does it (again); it tells you why when it cannot, and you can press it again once the cause is gone, for instance a program that holds a file open.
- **With the setup wizard.** Run `DatGoldSetup.exe`: when the folder you install into holds the marker, the wizard asks whether to repair it first and then installs.
- **With the repair form.** `DatGoldSetup.exe --quiet --recover --install-dir "<the DatGold folder>"` repairs the installation and nothing else. The setup is a Windows program with no console of its own, so a prompt that is just given the command shows nothing and does not wait: run it so that the shell waits and shows the line, for instance `.\DatGoldSetup.exe --quiet --recover --install-dir "<the DatGold folder>" 2>&1 | Out-Host; $LASTEXITCODE` in Windows PowerShell. It prints one line and exits 0 when the installation is whole (repaired, or there was nothing to repair) and 1 for everything else: the repair was refused (nothing was changed), it stopped halfway (run it again), a task runs or another update works on the folder, the folder is not there, or the arguments are wrong. It must be run from a DatGoldSetup.exe that is not in the DatGold folder; it takes no other argument.

The repair puts a file back only when it is the bytes the update wrote or the old ones, and removes a file the update created only when it is the bytes the update wrote. **It refuses, and changes nothing,** when it cannot prove that the installation is what the journal says: the backup is missing or damaged, `journal.json` cannot be read (setups up to 3.10.2 did not flush it to the disk), a file was changed by something else after the update began, or a name leads outside the installation or through a link. Nothing is put back outside the DatGold folder, and a name in the data folder of the Hub is refused; the only other things written are the repair's own log (in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ChatMCP\logs`, also when it refuses) and, in the window of an update, the result file. A stop in the middle (the power goes again, a file is held open) is repaired by running it again. After a repair made by the window of an update, the next start of DatGold says that the update did not go through (only that window writes the result file, and only when no program listens on port 3007: a repair made by the wizard or by `--recover`, or after a setup that was killed, leaves none, and DatGold then says nothing); a Hub that you start by hand, with `DATGOLD-HUB\START-CHATMCP-HUB.cmd` or `node hub.mjs`, leaves it alone while the marker is there, so it says nothing early. The repair was built for a rollback that could not finish and for a stop in the middle; it was run on what a commit killed in the middle leaves and by the lifecycle script on a disposable machine, and **not** after a real power cut or a real failed update.

**Recovering an installation by hand.** What can still be done when the repair above refuses because a file is neither what the update wrote nor what it replaced (somebody changed it, or an update that was cut off left it unfinished), and the only way for an older setup. It puts the installation back to what it was before the update whatever the files hold now, so read what it does first. Close DatGold, then run this in Windows PowerShell as the same user (set `$install` to the folder DatGold is installed in). It first checks that the journal lists something and that every backup is the file it was made from (the SHA-256 in the journal), and stops, changing nothing, when one is not: with a damaged backup there is nothing to put back from. Then it puts back every file the update replaced or removed from the backup folder of this installation, removes every file that the journal lists as created by the update, and removes the marker and the backup, so that DatGold and the setup work again:

~~~powershell
# recovery-from-retained-backup
$install = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\ChatMCP"
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$markerFile = Join-Path $install '.chatmcp-update-pending.json'
$named = ((Get-Content -LiteralPath $markerFile -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).backupDirectory).TrimEnd('\', '/')
$backups = Join-Path $install (Split-Path -Leaf $named)
$journal = Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $backups 'journal.json') -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
if (-not $journal) { throw 'The journal lists nothing. Nothing was changed.' }
foreach ($entry in $journal) {
    if ($entry.Backup) {
        $copy = Join-Path (Join-Path $backups 'old') (Split-Path -Leaf $entry.Backup)
        if ((Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $copy -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne $entry.OldHash) { throw "A backup is not the file it was made from: $($entry.Relative). Nothing was changed." }
    }
}
foreach ($entry in $journal) {
    $target = Join-Path $install ($entry.Relative -replace '/', '\')
    if ($entry.Backup) {
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Split-Path -Parent $target) | Out-Null
        Copy-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path (Join-Path $backups 'old') (Split-Path -Leaf $entry.Backup)) -Destination $target -Force
    } elseif (-not $entry.OldHash -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $target)) {
        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $target -Force
    }
}
Remove-Item -LiteralPath $markerFile -Force
Remove-Item -LiteralPath $backups -Recurse -Force
~~~

It stops at the first error. Up to the line that removes the marker nothing has been taken away, so it can be run again once the cause (a file that is open, say) is gone; after that line DatGold and the setup work again, and if the last line cannot remove the backup folder, that folder only takes up disk space and can be deleted by hand. It puts back what the journal lists: a file named like `<name>.<32 hexadecimal digits>.tmp` that a power cut left beside a file that was being replaced is not in the journal, and can be deleted by hand. The block is run for real on a retained backup by the native tests (`scripts/tests/native-lifecycle`), from this text, and by the lifecycle script (`scripts/tests/Test-NativeLifecycle.ps1`) on a disposable machine, which first checks that the real setup refuses to install behind the marker and refuses to repair a state in which a file was changed by something else, and then that the installation is whole again once the block has run. The repair of this section is run there too: in the real window of the update (the result file that it leaves and the old app that it opens again) and with the explicit form (twice).

To test the updater, build two versions that trust a key made for the run: `.\scripts\Build-Installer.ps1 -ReleaseKeysFile <full path of a key file>` builds that key list into the desktop shell and copies it over `DATGOLD-HUB\lib\release-keys.json` of the payload, so that the Hub the setup installs trusts the same list. The committed file is not touched, the script says that it is a test build, a publish workflow refuses the parameter, and the file must be a plain file of at most 16 KiB with an entry that says use `release` and a 91-byte key. The CI job "Windows in-app updater, end to end" does this for real on a hosted runner (`scripts/tests/updater-e2e/`): `Build-TestPair.ps1` builds an old and a newer setup of the commit under test side by side, with the versions given at build time and a key list that `scripts/new-release-key.mjs` made for the run, and `run.mjs` installs the old one, drives the page of the installed app with presses of the mouse that the browser takes for a person's (trusted clicks injected through the DevTools protocol, not the operating system's mouse), and lets the app update itself to the new one (a version is a plain `x.y.z`: the feed carries releases only, so a suffix such as `-test` is refused by the Hub and by the shell).

The installer and the uninstaller start Windows PowerShell as a child in two places: the helper that deletes `Uninstall.exe` once the uninstaller has ended, and the Hub ownership check of the preflight. Both go through `HubLifecycle.WindowsPowerShell` (`native-shared/HubLifecycle.cs`) and get no `PSModulePath`. A program started from a PowerShell 7 window hands PowerShell 7's module folders on, and Windows PowerShell would load them before its own and lose `Get-FileHash` (an uninstaller started that way used to leave `Uninstall.exe` behind). `scripts/tests/legacy-hub-upgrade/run.mjs` and `scripts/tests/Test-NativeLifecycle.ps1` start both from a stand-in for PowerShell 7's module folder, and `DATGOLD-HUB/tests/verify-native-hardening.mjs` keeps `HubLifecycle.cs` the only C# file that names `powershell.exe`.

before.scripts/Build-Installer.ps1:
#requires -Version 5.1
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Builds the commercial DatGoldSetup.exe standalone installer (called ChatMCPSetup.exe up to v3.10.2).

.DESCRIPTION
  Automated build pipeline:
  1. Generates official brand icons
  2. Compiles native desktop executable (ChatMCP.exe)
  3. Prepares distribution payload and compresses to installer/payload.zip
  4. Compiles and embeds payload into standalone dist/DatGoldSetup.exe

.PARAMETER ReleaseKeysFile
  TEST BUILDS ONLY. The full path of a key list that the desktop shell is built with and that the Hub it installs reads, instead of the committed
  DATGOLD-HUB\lib\release-keys.json (the end-to-end test of the updater builds two versions that trust a key made for the run). A release is built without it
  and a publish workflow refuses it.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [switch]$Force,
    [string]$ReleaseKeysFile = ''
)

Set-StrictMode -Version 2.0
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

Write-Host "==========================================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "            DatGold Studio - Installer Builder            " -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "==========================================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan

$scriptDir = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
$repoRoot = [IO.Path]::GetFullPath((Join-Path $scriptDir '..'))
. (Join-Path $scriptDir 'InstallerPayload.ps1')
$distDir = Join-Path $repoRoot 'dist'
$installerDir = Join-Path $repoRoot 'installer'
$temporaryRoot = [IO.Path]::GetFullPath($env:TEMP).TrimEnd('\', '/')
Assert-InstallerNoReparsePath -Path $temporaryRoot
# A release is built from the committed key list and from nothing else: a publish workflow whose environment names another one (MSBuild reads such a variable as a property) is stopped here.
Assert-InstallerNoAmbientReleaseKeysFile
if ($ReleaseKeysFile -ne '') {
    $ReleaseKeysFile = Resolve-InstallerReleaseKeysFile -Path $ReleaseKeysFile
    Write-Host "  [TEST BUILD] The release keys of this build are the ones in $ReleaseKeysFile, not the committed DATGOLD-HUB\lib\release-keys.json. Never publish what this builds." -ForegroundColor Yellow
}
$stagingDir = Join-Path $temporaryRoot ('ChatMCP-Staging-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))

# 1. Prerequisite checks
Write-Host "`n[1/5] Checking build prerequisites..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$dotnetCmd = Get-Command dotnet.exe -CommandType Application -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
if ($null -eq $dotnetCmd) {
    Write-Error ".NET SDK is required to build DatGoldSetup.exe. Please install from https://dot.net"
    exit 1
}
$dotnetVer = (& $dotnetCmd.Path --version).Trim()
Write-Host "  [OK] .NET SDK found: $dotnetVer" -ForegroundColor Green
if ([version]$dotnetVer -lt [version]'10.0') {
    throw ".NET SDK 10.0+ is required (desktop-shell and installer target net10.0-windows)."
}
$nodeCmd = Get-Command node.exe -CommandType Application -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
$npmCmd = Get-Command npm.cmd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
if ($null -eq $nodeCmd -or $null -eq $npmCmd) {
    throw "Node.js 22+ and npm are required to compile and package the offline frontend."
}
$null = Get-Command git.exe -CommandType Application -ErrorAction Stop
$nodeVersion = (& $nodeCmd.Path --version).Trim()
if ([version]($nodeVersion.TrimStart('v').Split('-')[0]) -lt [version]'22.0') {
    throw "Node.js 22+ is required; found $nodeVersion."
}
$hubManifest = Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $repoRoot 'DATGOLD-HUB\package.json') -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
[xml]$shellManifest = Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $repoRoot 'desktop-shell\ChatMCP.csproj') -Raw
[xml]$installerManifest = Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $repoRoot 'installer\ChatMCP.Installer.csproj') -Raw
if ($hubManifest.version -ne [string]$shellManifest.Project.PropertyGroup.Version -or
    $hubManifest.version -ne [string]$installerManifest.Project.PropertyGroup.Version) {
    throw "Version mismatch: Hub, Desktop and Installer must share one version before release."
}
Write-Host "  [OK] Node $nodeVersion and release version $($hubManifest.version)." -ForegroundColor Green

# Build the frontend from source. Packaging stale web/dist would make new
# React features invisible even when the backend and installer are updated.
Write-Host "  Building the latest offline React/TypeScript UI..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
Push-Location (Join-Path $repoRoot 'DATGOLD-HUB\ui')
try {
    & $npmCmd.Path ci --no-audit --no-fund
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "npm ci failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE" }
    & $npmCmd.Path run build
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Frontend build failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE" }
} finally {
    Pop-Location
}
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $repoRoot 'DATGOLD-HUB\web\dist\index.html') -PathType Leaf)) {
    throw "Built React UI not found at DATGOLD-HUB\web\dist\index.html."
}
Write-Host "  [OK] Fresh UI compiled and ready for packaging." -ForegroundColor Green

# 2. Brand Icons
Write-Host "`n[2/5] Ensuring brand icons..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$brandIcon = Join-Path $repoRoot 'assets\icons\chatmcp.ico'
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $brandIcon -PathType Leaf)) {
    $pythonCmd = Get-Command python.exe -CommandType Application -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($null -ne $pythonCmd) {
        Write-Host "  Rendering official brand icons..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
        & $pythonCmd.Path (Join-Path $repoRoot 'scripts\generate-brand-icon.py')
    }
}
Write-Host "  [OK] Brand icons ready." -ForegroundColor Green

# 3. Compile Native Desktop Shell (ChatMCP.exe)
Write-Host "`n[3/5] Compiling native desktop shell (ChatMCP.exe)..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $stagingDir) { throw "Private staging directory already exists: $stagingDir" }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $stagingDir | Out-Null
try {
$shellCsproj = Join-Path $repoRoot 'desktop-shell\ChatMCP.csproj'
$shellDist = Join-Path $stagingDir 'desktop-publish'
$payloadDir = Join-Path $stagingDir 'payload'
# The key list is built into the program (desktop-shell/ShellKeys.cs): the one that is committed, unless this is a test build that names another. It is ALWAYS named on the command line and never
# left to the default of the project: MSBuild reads environment variables as properties, so a variable called ReleaseKeysFile in the environment of a release build would otherwise be the list the program trusts.
$shellKeysFile = if ($ReleaseKeysFile -ne '') { $ReleaseKeysFile } else { Join-Path $repoRoot 'DATGOLD-HUB\lib\release-keys.json' }
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $shellKeysFile -PathType Leaf)) { throw "The release key list is not a file: $shellKeysFile" }
# (written so that MSBuild reads the path back as it is: a repository in C:\My Repos, Inc\ or C:\a;b\ must build as well)
$shellKeysArgument = ConvertTo-InstallerMsbuildValue -Value $shellKeysFile
Invoke-InstallerBuildStep -Description 'Desktop publish' -Command { & $dotnetCmd.Path publish $shellCsproj -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true -o $shellDist -p:PublishSingleFile=true "-p:ReleaseKeysFile=$shellKeysArgument" }
$desktopExe = Join-Path $shellDist 'ChatMCP.exe'
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $desktopExe -PathType Leaf)) {
    throw "Failed to compile desktop shell: $desktopExe not found."
}
Write-Host "  [OK] Compiled ChatMCP.exe: $([Math]::Round((Get-Item $desktopExe).Length / 1MB, 2)) MB" -ForegroundColor Green
# Not believed, proved: the program that came out holds the exact bytes of the key list this build meant to give it (the resource is the file, byte for byte), whatever the way it was asked for.
Assert-InstallerReleaseKeysBuiltIn -Executable $desktopExe -KeysFile $shellKeysFile
Write-Host "  [OK] ChatMCP.exe carries the key list $shellKeysFile, byte for byte." -ForegroundColor Green

# 4. Prepare Staging & Build Payload Zip
Write-Host "`n[4/5] Packaging payload archive..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
# Both the executable and a valid x64 WebView2 loader are mandatory. A reused
# publish folder can silently omit native files on incremental publish.
Copy-InstallerDesktopPayload -PublishDirectory $shellDist -Destination $payloadDir

# Copy tracked runtime source files and the freshly generated UI only. Never
# recurse over source folders: ignored files may contain private user state.
Copy-InstallerSourcePayload -RepositoryRoot $repoRoot -Destination $payloadDir
if ($ReleaseKeysFile -ne '') {
    # The Hub reads its keys from the installed files, the shell has them built in: both must trust the same list (this copy comes after the tracked files, which it replaces).
    Copy-Item -LiteralPath $ReleaseKeysFile -Destination (Join-Path $payloadDir 'CHATMCP-HUB\lib\release-keys.json') -Force
}
# and proved again after the last copy that could change it: the Hub of the payload reads the same list as the shell.
Assert-InstallerReleaseKeysShipped -PayloadDirectory $payloadDir -KeysFile $shellKeysFile
Write-Host "  [OK] The Hub in the payload reads the same key list." -ForegroundColor Green

# Trusted Sandbox Supervisor: publish from checked source into a fresh private
# staging directory. Never recursively package GuestSupervisor bin/obj/source.
# This binary does not make OS isolation available until the production
# broker authenticates published guest results and the dedicated gate passes.
$supervisorProject = Join-Path $repoRoot 'DATGOLD-HUB\windows\sandbox\GuestSupervisor\GuestSupervisor.csproj'
$supervisorPublish = Join-Path $stagingDir 'supervisor-publish'
Invoke-InstallerBuildStep -Description 'GuestSupervisor publish' -Command { & $dotnetCmd.Path publish $supervisorProject -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true -p:PublishAot=true -p:PublishSingleFile=false -o $supervisorPublish }
$trustedSupervisor = Join-Path $supervisorPublish 'GuestSupervisor.exe'
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trustedSupervisor -PathType Leaf)) { throw 'Published GuestSupervisor.exe is missing.' }
$supervisorSize = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $trustedSupervisor).Length
if ($supervisorSize -le 0) { throw 'Published GuestSupervisor.exe is empty.' }
# Exercise the exact AOT image being packaged. This inert native parser suite
# never starts a guest and does not attest Sandbox isolation.
& $trustedSupervisor --blackbox-grader-self-test
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Published GuestSupervisor native grader self-test failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE" }
$trustedDestination = Join-Path $payloadDir 'CHATMCP-HUB\runtimes\windows-sandbox'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $trustedDestination -Force | Out-Null
Copy-Item -LiteralPath $trustedSupervisor -Destination (Join-Path $trustedDestination 'GuestSupervisor.exe') -Force

  and a publish workflow refuses it.

    [string]$ReleaseKeysFile = ''
)

Write-Host "            DatGold Studio - Installer Builder            " -ForegroundColor Cyan

| Vendored file | Upstream project | Compiled into |
|---|---|---|
| `tree-sitter-javascript.LICENSE` | <https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-javascript> | `grammars/tree-sitter-javascript.wasm` |
| `tree-sitter-typescript.LICENSE` | <https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-typescript> | `grammars/tree-sitter-typescript.wasm`, `grammars/tree-sitter-tsx.wasm` |
| `tree-sitter-python.LICENSE` | <https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-python> | `grammars/tree-sitter-python.wasm` |

Each file is the project's own `LICENSE` file, copied unchanged from the upstream repository (`tree-sitter-wasms` 0.1.13 declares `^0.20.3`, `^0.20.5` and `^0.21.0` as the development dependencies it built the grammars from; the exact versions are not recorded in the package). These three files were copied unchanged from the default branch of each upstream repository on 2026-10-19 (`gh api repos/tree-sitter/<project>/contents/LICENSE`): tree-sitter-javascript (Copyright (c) 2014 Max Brunsfeld), tree-sitter-typescript (2017 Max Brunsfeld), tree-sitter-python (2016 Max Brunsfeld). The upstream default branch may be newer than the grammar builds inside `tree-sitter-wasms` 0.1.13; the copyright lines of these projects have not changed, but the grammar versions are not recorded in the package.

If one of them is missing or unusable:

## What is compiled into rg.exe (`ripgrep/`)

`rg.exe` is staged from the official ripgrep archive by `stage-ripgrep.ps1`. The archive carries the texts of ripgrep itself (`LICENSE-MIT`, `UNLICENSE`, `COPYING`) and nothing else, but the binary is statically linked with PCRE2 (BSD-3-Clause, which asks for its notice in binary redistributions), with Rust crates and with the Rust standard library of the toolchain that built it. Their texts are vendored in `ripgrep/`, and `stage.mjs` copies them, with the inventory, to `licenses/ripgrep/` in the staged runtime, which `Build-Installer.ps1` ships as `CHATMCP-HUB/licenses/ripgrep/`.

A component's license expression decides which kinds it needs (`MIT OR Apache-2.0` needs both texts; an identifier that `notices.mjs` does not know is an error).

The dependencies of each package (kind, `cfg(...)` target, optional, features) come from that index and from ripgrep's workspace manifests; the normal dependencies of the `ripgrep` package, with the `pcre2` feature, for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (`windows`, `target_env = "msvc"`, `crt-static`, release profile), were followed with Cargo's feature rules. - The list comes from the sources of the release. `rg.exe` was not opened when it was derived; what the installer build checks against it is the PCRE2 version string and what `rg --pcre2-version` prints, nothing about the crates. A crate that the build links but that the rules above miss would be missing here.

### Deriving it again for a new ripgrep release

1. Change the pin in `stage-ripgrep.ps1` (version, URL, SHA-256). Staging and `tests/verify-notices.mjs` fail until the inventory belongs to it.
2. Repeat steps 1 to 4 above for the new tag, and step 5 for the toolchain of its release run (the toolchain is the first thing that changes; a new Rust brings new crates and new in-tree notices: read `REUSE.toml`, `license-metadata.json` and `library/Cargo.lock` again), rewrite `ripgrep/` (texts and `MANIFEST.json`), and update the rows in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` and `DATGOLD-HUB/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` and the paths of `guest-lifecycle.ps1`. `node DATGOLD-HUB/tests/verify-notices.mjs` names what is left. The scripts used on 2026-10-25 are not part of the repository.

1. **The build.** `.github/workflows/release.yml` at tag 15.2.0 builds the Windows binary with `cargo build --profile release-lto --features pcre2 --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and `PCRE2_SYS_STATIC=1`; `.cargo/config.toml` adds `-C target-feature=+crt-static`.
2. **The crates.** ripgrep's `Cargo.lock` at the tag has 59 packages (`basis.lockfile`: commit, blob id, SHA-256). The checksum of every registry package equals the one in the crates.io index. The dependencies of each package (kind, `cfg(...)` target, optional, features) come from that index and from ripgrep's workspace manifests; the normal dependencies of the `ripgrep` package, with the `pcre2` feature, for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (`windows`, `target_env = "msvc"`, `crt-static`, release profile), were followed with Cargo's feature rules. Result: 10 workspace crates, 30 registry crates and 19 packages that are not linked (development and build dependencies such as `regex` and `cc`, optional crates no feature reaches, `tikv-jemallocator` for musl only).
3. **PCRE2.** `pcre2-sys` 0.2.10 bundles the sources and its `update-pcre2` fetches PCRE2 10.46; `include/pcre2.h` in the crate says `PCRE2_MAJOR 10`, `PCRE2_MINOR 46`. The crate does not bundle PCRE2's license, so the text is `LICENCE.md` of PCRE2Project/pcre2 at tag `pcre2-10.46` (the same bytes as at `pcre2-10.45`). Note that `rg --pcre2-version` prints `PCRE2 10.45`, not 10.46: `pcre2::version()` returns the `PCRE2_MAJOR` and `PCRE2_MINOR` constants of `pcre2-sys/src/bindings.rs`, which were generated for 10.45 and not regenerated when the bundled sources went to 10.46. The installer build of the first version of this inventory (derived from the sources alone) stopped on exactly that, which is why the inventory records both numbers (`rgReports`: what rg prints; `compiledVersionString`: what the compiled library carries, `pcre2_config.c` builds it from `pcre2.h`) and why the check that ties the notice to the binary is the search for the second one in the bytes of `rg.exe`. The number it prints also says which `pcre2-sys` built the binary: the bindings and the bundled sources agree in 0.2.8 (42) and 0.2.9 (43) and only 0.2.10 has 45 against 46, so a binary that prints 10.45 was built with 0.2.10, the version in the lock. The technique of the byte search was tried first on another MSVC build of ripgrep with PCRE2 (a copy bundled with an editor): its `.rdata` carries the same literal, once.
4. **The texts.** For each crate, the license files of the upstream repository named on crates.io, at the commit of the tag of that version (`windows-sys` and `windows-link` have no tag: the windows-rs commit "Release 71" that set these versions), read through the git objects with the GitHub API; the git blob id was recomputed from the bytes. Beyond the files at the top of a crate's folder: the Unicode license of `bstr`, `regex-syntax` and `regex-automata`, and the license of the C++ project that `zmij` ports.
5. **The Rust standard library (`rustStd`).** ripgrep's release workflow builds with `nightly` and does not pin it: there is no `rust-toolchain` file at the tag and the `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master` step requests no components. `rustStd.toolchain` records what the release record says: run 29431117779, job `build-release (win-msvc, windows-latest, nightly, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)` started 2026-07-15T16:07:59Z; the nightly manifests `dist/<date>/channel-rust-nightly.toml` were published 2026-07-14 01:27:58Z, 2026-07-15 01:29:39Z and 2026-07-16 01:30:20Z, so `nightly` was the one of 2026-07-15, whose `[pkg.rustc]` says `version = "1.99.0-nightly (da80ed070 2026-07-14)"` and `git_commit_hash = "da80ed0708a09dc096c184345d6eb42cbcd50a1e"`. The toolchain was not downloaded; the texts of rust-lang/rust were read through the git objects of that commit. Rust's `COPYRIGHT` there lists no third-party text: it says that licenses are tracked with REUSE (`REUSE.toml`, `license-metadata.json`, the cached output of the `reuse` tool, and `LICENSES/`) and with cargo, and that `src/tools/generate-copyright` collects both into `COPYRIGHT-library.html`, which ships only in the `rustc` component of a toolchain (bootstrap `dist.rs`) and was not downloaded. So the inventory is built from the same inputs. Under `library/`, `license-metadata.json` names the Unicode tables of `core` (Unicode-3.0), `backtrace` (a git submodule: its texts are those of the pinned commit of rust-lang/backtrace-rs), `std/src/sync/mpmc` (the copyright of The Crossbeam Project Developers: the texts are crossbeam's, at the tag `crossbeam-channel-0.5.17`) and a Fuchsia mutex that is not compiled for Windows; the subtrees `compiler-builtins` (with `libm`), `stdarch` and `portable-simd` carry license files of their own. The registry crates that `std` links for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc were read from `library/std/Cargo.toml`, `library/sysroot/Cargo.toml`, `library/unwind/Cargo.toml`, `library/compiler-builtins/compiler-builtins/Cargo.toml` and `library/Cargo.lock` (49 packages): `cfg-if`, `hashbrown` and `rustc-demangle`. `libc`, `miniz_oxide`, `addr2line`, `object` (and so `gimli`, `adler2`, `memchr`) are gated off for this target, where backtraces use `dbghelp`; `foldhash` is reached only through a feature that `std` switches off. The locked checksums of the three linked crates equal the crates.io index. The 27 other registry packages are in `rustStd.notLinked` with the reason.
6. **The Microsoft C/C++ runtime components.** The terms were read on 2026-10-25 and are summarised in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` (section "Microsoft C/C++ runtime components"); no Microsoft text is vendored. What was read, with the file hashes: the license terms of the Windows SDK as installed with SDK 10.0.26100.0 and 10.0.28000.0 (`Windows Kits\10\Licenses\<version>\sdk_license.rtf`, identical, SHA-256 `0f4a26ac9dc50066f8a1bfeaaf3f092d1b9e4791df5487b9f3c31e7c3dc4d7f5`) and the REDIST.TXT list <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/legal/windows-sdk/redist> (updated 2024-10-21; section "Static LIB files"); the Visual Studio 2022 Enterprise and Professional terms (<https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/Visual-Studio-2022-Enterprise-Professional-License-EN.docx>, SHA-256 `9c0cd52b20db9d081854c75bd1b50c75514b8f8cb09c8cad15e89d90b97b5bf3`) and Visual Studio 2026 terms (<https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Visual_Studio_2026-License-Enterprise_Professional_ENU.docx>, last updated 2025-10-01, SHA-256 `dd2ab92a7c2bb90dd509e16572707a34b13bc0bc09b9199d115f25594ac39053`), section "Distributable Code"; the Distributable Lists of Visual Studio 2022 and 2026 (<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/releases/2022/redistribution>, <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/releases/2026/redistribution>, both dated 2025-11-11); "Redistribute Visual C++ Files" (ms.date 2026-04-13); "C runtime (CRT) and C++ standard library (STL) lib files" (ms.date 2021-03-05), which says that `libcmt.lib`, `libvcruntime.lib` and `libucrt.lib` are the statically linked CRT of `/MT` and that the static library of the UCRT is in the Windows SDK; and the license of the redistributable package (<https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/Visual-C-Runtime-2015-2022-License-1.docx>, SHA-256 `f1e3d56ceb2ad68aae0711b910375009e651ac5530fa0760f0dea6e81e54fae1`). The maintainer decided on 2026-10-25 to name the components and summarise the terms without reproducing them.

### What this does not cover

- The toolchain is derived from the release record and the nightly manifests, not read from the binary: the first time the inventory meets `rg.exe` is `checkCompiledRust` in the installer build, which fails (and names the commits that the binary carries) when the guess is wrong. The same holds for the Rust crates and the in-tree parts: they come from manifests, so a crate that the build links but that the rules above miss would be missing here, and `/rust/deps/<crate>-<version>/` paths in the binary would show it. The Microsoft terms are summarised, not reproduced, and what they mean for DatGold as a redistributor is a legal question that `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` states and does not answer.
- The list comes from the sources of the release. `rg.exe` was not opened when it was derived; what the installer build checks against it is the PCRE2 version string and what `rg --pcre2-version` prints, nothing about the crates. A crate that the build links but that the rules above miss would be missing here.
- These are inventories kept by the maintainers, not legal advice.

### Deriving it again for a new ripgrep release

1. Change the pin in `stage-ripgrep.ps1` (version, URL, SHA-256). Staging and `tests/verify-notices.mjs` fail until the inventory belongs to it.
2. Repeat steps 1 to 4 above for the new tag, and step 5 for the toolchain of its release run (the toolchain is the first thing that changes; a new Rust brings new crates and new in-tree notices: read `REUSE.toml`, `license-metadata.json` and `library/Cargo.lock` again), rewrite `ripgrep/` (texts and `MANIFEST.json`), and update the rows in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` and `DATGOLD-HUB/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` and the paths of `guest-lifecycle.ps1`. `node DATGOLD-HUB/tests/verify-notices.mjs` names what is left. The scripts used on 2026-10-25 are not part of the repository.

+# Publish only the user-authorized release commit. All gates use that exact SHA.
+# v3.11.1 is a normal release: it is published as the "latest" release, after the same gates as v3.11.0. The downloads are DatGoldSetup.exe and DatGold-Browser-Companion.zip (the old-named ChatMCP-Browser-Companion.zip is no longer published, on the owner's instruction of 2026-10-28). +name: Publish ChatMCP v3.11.1
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+concurrency:
+  group: publish-chatmcp-v3.11.1-${{ github.sha }}
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+jobs:
+  browser:
+    name: Real Chromium MV3 delivery gate
+    if: >-
+      ${{ startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'release: ChatMCP v3.11.1') }}
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 20
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020
+        with:
+          node-version: '24'
+      - name: Run actual extension IPC on scripted pages, without live login
+        working-directory: DATGOLD-HUB/ui
+        env:
+          PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_FILE: ${{ runner.temp }}/companion-release-evidence/results.json
+        run: |
+          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/companion-release-evidence"
+          npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
+          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
+          npx playwright test e2e/companion-ipc.spec.mjs --workers=1 --reporter=line,json
+      - name: Preserve browser evidence
+        if: always()
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
+        with:
+          name: ChatMCP-v3.11.1-browser-evidence
+          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/companion-release-evidence
+          if-no-files-found: error
+  windows:
+    name: Build and test installed Windows upgrade
+    if: >-
+      ${{ startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'release: ChatMCP v3.11.1') }}
+    runs-on: windows-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 75
+    defaults:
+      run:
+        shell: pwsh
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
+          fetch-depth: 0
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020
+        with:
+          node-version: '24'
+      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@67a3573c9a986a3f9c594539f4ab511d57bb3ce9
+        with:
+          dotnet-version: '10.0.x'
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065
+        with:
+          python-version: '3.11'
+      - name: Guard exact commit and all component versions
+        run: |
+          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
+          New-Item -ItemType Directory "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence" -Force | Out-Null
+          $env:GITHUB_SHA | Set-Content "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/commit.txt" -Encoding utf8
+          if ((git rev-parse HEAD).Trim() -ne $env:GITHUB_SHA) { throw 'Wrong checkout' }
+          if ((git show -s --format=%s HEAD).Trim() -ne 'release: ChatMCP v3.11.1') { throw 'Wrong release commit' }
+          foreach ($file in @('DATGOLD-HUB/package.json','DATGOLD-HUB/ui/package.json','DATGOLD-HUB/ui/package-lock.json')) {
+            if ((Get-Content $file -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable)['version'] -ne '3.11.1') { throw "Version mismatch: $file" }
+          }
+          foreach ($file in @('desktop-shell/ChatMCP.csproj','installer/ChatMCP.Installer.csproj')) {
+            if (-not (Get-Content $file -Raw).Contains('<Version>3.11.1</Version>')) { throw "Native version mismatch: $file" }
+          }
+          if ((Get-Content DATGOLD-HUB/extension/manifest.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).version -ne '1.5.2') { throw 'Companion version mismatch' }
+          if (-not (Test-Path RELEASE-NOTES-v3.11.1.md)) { throw 'Missing release notes' }
+      - name: Native health, ownership and transactional rollback regression
+        run: |
+          python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p test_release_source.py -v
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Release source provenance regression failed' }
+          dotnet run --project scripts/tests/native-lifecycle/NativeLifecycle.Tests.csproj --configuration Release 2>&1 | Tee-Object "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/native-unit.log"
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Native unit regression failed' }
+          powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/Test-InstallerPayload.ps1
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Installer payload regression failed' }
+      - name: Complete no-skip Hub regression
+        run: |
+          python -m pip install -r DATGOLD-HUB/tests/requirements-e2e.txt
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Dependency installation failed' }
+          git config --global user.email 'ci@example.invalid'
+          git config --global user.name 'ci'
+          node DATGOLD-HUB/tests/run-all.mjs --no-skip all --json "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/node-summary.json" 2>&1 | Tee-Object "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/node-all.log"
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Hub regression failed' }
+      - name: Build fresh versioned Windows installer
+        run: |
+          powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/Build-Installer.ps1 2>&1 | Tee-Object "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/build.log"
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Installer build failed' }
+      - name: Retrieve published hash-pinned upgrade baseline
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+        run: |
+          gh release download v3.9.0 --repo $env:GITHUB_REPOSITORY --pattern ChatMCPSetup.exe --dir "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-baseline"
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Baseline download failed' }
+          if ((Get-FileHash "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-baseline/ChatMCPSetup.exe" -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne 'ef75e9a3721c5ba94a510de1ff00c1449031a4ac797570cb0d901861b509786e') { throw 'Baseline checksum mismatch' }
+      - name: Real setup upgrade, installed EXE lifecycle and uninstall
+        run: |
+          powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/tests/Test-NativeLifecycle.ps1 -BaselineInstaller "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-baseline/ChatMCPSetup.exe" -CandidateInstaller dist/DatGoldSetup.exe -ExpectedBaselineVersion 3.9.0 -ExpectedCandidateVersion 3.11.1 -OutputDirectory "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/installed-lifecycle"
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Installed EXE acceptance failed' }
+      - name: Native WebView2 smoke and canonical Companion parity
+        run: |
+          node DATGOLD-HUB/ui/e2e/webview2-smoke.mjs
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'WebView2 smoke failed' }
+          powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/Build-BrowserCompanion.ps1 -VerifyInstallerPayload
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Companion source/ZIP/payload parity failed' }
+      - name: Verify final asset checksums and record provenance
+        run: |
+          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
+          $assets = @()
+          foreach ($name in @('DatGoldSetup.exe','DatGold-Browser-Companion.zip')) {
+            $file = Join-Path dist $name
+            $actual = (Get-FileHash $file -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
+            $expected = ((Get-Content "$file.sha256" -Raw).Trim() -split '\s+')[0].ToLowerInvariant()
+            if ($actual -ne $expected) { throw "Checksum mismatch: $name" }
+            $assets += [ordered]@{ name=$name; sha256=$actual; bytes=(Get-Item $file).Length }
+          }
+          $native = Get-Content "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/installed-lifecycle/report.json" -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
+          if ($native.result -ne 'PASS' -or $native.candidateSha256 -ne $assets[0].sha256) { throw 'Native evidence does not match the release EXE' }
+          [ordered]@{ version='3.11.1'; companionVersion='1.5.2'; commit=$env:GITHUB_SHA; workflowRun=$env:GITHUB_RUN_ID; assets=$assets; signedInEdgeVerified=$false; authenticodeSigned=$false } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6 | Set-Content dist/RELEASE-MANIFEST.json -Encoding utf8
+          python scripts/verify-release-source.py --commit "$env:GITHUB_SHA" --evidence "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence"
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Source or generated-UI payload provenance verification failed' }
+      - name: Upload tested release files
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
+        with:
+          name: ChatMCP-v3.11.1-Windows-and-Companion
+          path: |
+            dist/DatGoldSetup.exe
+            dist/DatGoldSetup.exe.sha256
+            dist/DatGold-Browser-Companion.zip
+            dist/DatGold-Browser-Companion.zip.sha256
+            dist/RELEASE-MANIFEST.json
+          if-no-files-found: error
+      - name: Preserve actual Windows evidence even on failure
+        if: always()
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
+        with:
+          name: ChatMCP-v3.11.1-native-evidence
+          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/native-release-evidence
+          if-no-files-found: error
+  publish:
+    name: Publish verified v3.11.1 release
+    needs: [browser, windows]
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 20
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+      actions: read
+    env:
+      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+      TAG: v3.11.1
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
+          fetch-depth: 0
+      - name: Require regular CI success on this exact release commit
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          for attempt in $(seq 1 60); do
+            result=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$GITHUB_SHA&event=push&per_page=100" --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.path == ".github/workflows/ci.yml")][0] | [.status // "missing", .conclusion // "none"] | @tsv')
+            read -r status conclusion <<< "$result"
+            if [ "$status" = completed ]; then
+              test "$conclusion" = success || { echo "CI ended: $conclusion"; exit 1; }
+              exit 0
+            fi
+            sleep 15
+          done
+          echo 'CI did not finish successfully before publication deadline'; exit 1
+      - name: Retrieve only artifacts from this successful workflow run
+        run: |
+          gh run download "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --name ChatMCP-v3.11.1-Windows-and-Companion --dir dist
+          python - <<'PY'
+          import hashlib, json, os
+          from pathlib import Path
+          root = Path('dist')
+          manifest = json.loads((root / 'RELEASE-MANIFEST.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig'))
+          assert manifest['commit'] == os.environ['GITHUB_SHA']
+          assert manifest['version'] == '3.11.1' and manifest['companionVersion'] == '1.5.2'
+          assert {a['name'] for a in manifest['assets']} == {'DatGoldSetup.exe', 'DatGold-Browser-Companion.zip'}
+          for asset in manifest['assets']:
+              file = root / asset['name']
+              assert file.stat().st_size == asset['bytes']
+              digest = hashlib.file_digest(file.open('rb'), 'sha256').hexdigest()
+              assert digest == asset['sha256']
+              assert digest == (root / (asset['name'] + '.sha256')).read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig').split()[0]
+          print('Exact-commit release asset hashes verified again before publication.')
+          PY
+      - name: Publish version tag without moving existing tags and release assets
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          test "$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)" = "$GITHUB_SHA" || { echo 'main moved; refusing stale publication'; exit 1; }
+          if git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+            git fetch origin "refs/tags/$TAG:refs/tags/$TAG"
+            test "$(git rev-list -n1 "$TAG")" = "$GITHUB_SHA" || { echo 'Tag points at another commit'; exit 1; }
+          else
+            git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
+            git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
+            git tag -a "$TAG" -m 'DatGold v3.11.1 - skills chosen from the project, bigger attachments and a compaction you can tune' "$GITHUB_SHA"
+            git push origin "refs/tags/$TAG"
+          fi
+          gh release create "$TAG" dist/DatGoldSetup.exe dist/DatGoldSetup.exe.sha256 dist/DatGold-Browser-Companion.zip dist/DatGold-Browser-Companion.zip.sha256 dist/RELEASE-MANIFEST.json --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --verify-tag --draft --title 'DatGold v3.11.1 - skills chosen from the project, bigger attachments and a compaction you can tune' --notes-file RELEASE-NOTES-v3.11.1.md
+          gh release edit "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --draft=false --latest

  windows:
    name: Build and test installed Windows upgrade
    if: >-
      ${{ startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'release: ChatMCP v3.11.1') }}
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 75
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: pwsh
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020
        with:
          node-version: '24'
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@67a3573c9a986a3f9c594539f4ab511d57bb3ce9
        with:
          dotnet-version: '10.0.x'
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Guard exact commit and all component versions
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          New-Item -ItemType Directory "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence" -Force | Out-Null
          $env:GITHUB_SHA | Set-Content "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/commit.txt" -Encoding utf8
          if ((git rev-parse HEAD).Trim() -ne $env:GITHUB_SHA) { throw 'Wrong checkout' }
          if ((git show -s --format=%s HEAD).Trim() -ne 'release: ChatMCP v3.11.1') { throw 'Wrong release commit' }
          foreach ($file in @('DATGOLD-HUB/package.json','DATGOLD-HUB/ui/package.json','DATGOLD-HUB/ui/package-lock.json')) {
            if ((Get-Content $file -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable)['version'] -ne '3.11.1') { throw "Version mismatch: $file" }
          }
          foreach ($file in @('desktop-shell/ChatMCP.csproj','installer/ChatMCP.Installer.csproj')) {
            if (-not (Get-Content $file -Raw).Contains('<Version>3.11.1</Version>')) { throw "Native version mismatch: $file" }
          }
          if ((Get-Content DATGOLD-HUB/extension/manifest.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).version -ne '1.5.2') { throw 'Companion version mismatch' }
          if (-not (Test-Path RELEASE-NOTES-v3.11.1.md)) { throw 'Missing release notes' }
      - name: Native health, ownership and transactional rollback regression
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p test_release_source.py -v
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Release source provenance regression failed' }
          dotnet run --project scripts/tests/native-lifecycle/NativeLifecycle.Tests.csproj --configuration Release 2>&1 | Tee-Object "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/native-unit.log"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Native unit regression failed' }
          powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/Test-InstallerPayload.ps1
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Installer payload regression failed' }
      - name: Complete no-skip Hub regression
        run: |
          python -m pip install -r DATGOLD-HUB/tests/requirements-e2e.txt
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Dependency installation failed' }
          git config --global user.email 'ci@example.invalid'
          git config --global user.name 'ci'
          node DATGOLD-HUB/tests/run-all.mjs --no-skip all --json "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/node-summary.json" 2>&1 | Tee-Object "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/node-all.log"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Hub regression failed' }
      - name: Build fresh versioned Windows installer
        run: |
          powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/Build-Installer.ps1 2>&1 | Tee-Object "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/build.log"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Installer build failed' }
      - name: Retrieve published hash-pinned upgrade baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh release download v3.9.0 --repo $env:GITHUB_REPOSITORY --pattern ChatMCPSetup.exe --dir "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-baseline"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Baseline download failed' }
          if ((Get-FileHash "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-baseline/ChatMCPSetup.exe" -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne 'ef75e9a3721c5ba94a510de1ff00c1449031a4ac797570cb0d901861b509786e') { throw 'Baseline checksum mismatch' }
      - name: Real setup upgrade, installed EXE lifecycle and uninstall
        run: |
          powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/tests/Test-NativeLifecycle.ps1 -BaselineInstaller "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-baseline/ChatMCPSetup.exe" -CandidateInstaller dist/DatGoldSetup.exe -ExpectedBaselineVersion 3.9.0 -ExpectedCandidateVersion 3.11.1 -OutputDirectory "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/installed-lifecycle"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Installed EXE acceptance failed' }
      - name: Native WebView2 smoke and canonical Companion parity
        run: |
          node DATGOLD-HUB/ui/e2e/webview2-smoke.mjs
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'WebView2 smoke failed' }
          powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/Build-BrowserCompanion.ps1 -VerifyInstallerPayload
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Companion source/ZIP/payload parity failed' }
      - name: Verify final asset checksums and record provenance
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          $assets = @()
          foreach ($name in @('DatGoldSetup.exe','DatGold-Browser-Companion.zip')) {
            $file = Join-Path dist $name
            $actual = (Get-FileHash $file -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
            $expected = ((Get-Content "$file.sha256" -Raw).Trim() -split '\s+')[0].ToLowerInvariant()
            if ($actual -ne $expected) { throw "Checksum mismatch: $name" }
            $assets += [ordered]@{ name=$name; sha256=$actual; bytes=(Get-Item $file).Length }
          }
          $native = Get-Content "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/installed-lifecycle/report.json" -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
          if ($native.result -ne 'PASS' -or $native.candidateSha256 -ne $assets[0].sha256) { throw 'Native evidence does not match the release EXE' }
          [ordered]@{ version='3.11.1'; companionVersion='1.5.2'; commit=$env:GITHUB_SHA; workflowRun=$env:GITHUB_RUN_ID; assets=$assets; signedInEdgeVerified=$false; authenticodeSigned=$false } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6 | Set-Content dist/RELEASE-MANIFEST.json -Encoding utf8
          python scripts/verify-release-source.py --commit "$env:GITHUB_SHA" --evidence "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Source or generated-UI payload provenance verification failed' }
      - name: Upload tested release files
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
        with:
          name: ChatMCP-v3.11.1-Windows-and-Companion
          path: |
            dist/DatGoldSetup.exe
            dist/DatGoldSetup.exe.sha256
            dist/DatGold-Browser-Companion.zip
            dist/DatGold-Browser-Companion.zip.sha256
            dist/RELEASE-MANIFEST.json
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Preserve actual Windows evidence even on failure
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
        with:
          name: ChatMCP-v3.11.1-native-evidence
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/native-release-evidence
          if-no-files-found: error
  publish:
    name: Publish verified v3.11.1 release
    needs: [browser, windows]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: read
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      TAG: v3.11.1
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Require regular CI success on this exact release commit
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for attempt in $(seq 1 60); do
            result=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$GITHUB_SHA&event=push&per_page=100" --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.path == ".github/workflows/ci.yml")][0] | [.status // "missing", .conclusion // "none"] | @tsv')
            read -r status conclusion <<< "$result"
            if [ "$status" = completed ]; then
              test "$conclusion" = success || { echo "CI ended: $conclusion"; exit 1; }
              exit 0
            fi
            sleep 15
          done
          echo 'CI did not finish successfully before publication deadline'; exit 1
      - name: Retrieve only artifacts from this successful workflow run
        run: |
          gh run download "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --name ChatMCP-v3.11.1-Windows-and-Companion --dir dist
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib, json, os
          from pathlib import Path
          root = Path('dist')
          manifest = json.loads((root / 'RELEASE-MANIFEST.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig'))
          assert manifest['commit'] == os.environ['GITHUB_SHA']
          assert manifest['version'] == '3.11.1' and manifest['companionVersion'] == '1.5.2'
          assert {a['name'] for a in manifest['assets']} == {'DatGoldSetup.exe', 'DatGold-Browser-Companion.zip'}
          for asset in manifest['assets']:
              file = root / asset['name']
              assert file.stat().st_size == asset['bytes']
              digest = hashlib.file_digest(file.open('rb'), 'sha256').hexdigest()
              assert digest == asset['sha256']
              assert digest == (root / (asset['name'] + '.sha256')).read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig').split()[0]
          print('Exact-commit release asset hashes verified again before publication.')
          PY
      - name: Publish version tag without moving existing tags and release assets
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          test "$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)" = "$GITHUB_SHA" || { echo 'main moved; refusing stale publication'; exit 1; }
          if git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            git fetch origin "refs/tags/$TAG:refs/tags/$TAG"
            test "$(git rev-list -n1 "$TAG")" = "$GITHUB_SHA" || { echo 'Tag points at another commit'; exit 1; }
          else
            git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
            git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
            git tag -a "$TAG" -m 'DatGold v3.11.1 - skills chosen from the project, bigger attachments and a compaction you can tune' "$GITHUB_SHA"
            git push origin "refs/tags/$TAG"
          fi
          gh release create "$TAG" dist/DatGoldSetup.exe dist/DatGoldSetup.exe.sha256 dist/DatGold-Browser-Companion.zip dist/DatGold-Browser-Companion.zip.sha256 dist/RELEASE-MANIFEST.json --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --verify-tag --draft --title 'DatGold v3.11.1 - skills chosen from the project, bigger attachments and a compaction you can tune' --notes-file RELEASE-NOTES-v3.11.1.md
          gh release edit "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --draft=false --latest

# ChatMCP Agent — hai chế độ (Hub 1.2.0)

## Mục tiêu

Từ dashboard `http://127.0.0.1:3007`, chọn **ChatGPT Web** hoặc **API Gateway** rồi giao tác vụ tới các công cụ MCP thực tế đang kết nối vào workspace Windows. Hub hiển thị tiến độ theo từng lượt, tên và tham số công cụ (bản xem trước), kết quả/lỗi MCP, số lượt và báo cáo cuối; cập nhật khoảng 2 giây. Trường **progress** (Web) hoặc lời ghi chú ngắn do model cung cấp (API) là **tóm tắt hành động cho người dùng**, KHÔNG phải chuỗi suy luận nội bộ của mô hình.

| | ChatGPT Web | API Gateway |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nguồn model | ChatGPT web đang đăng nhập | Gateway do người dùng cấu hình |
| API key | Không cần | Cần key riêng |
| Companion | Cần, phiên bản 1.3.7 | Không cần |
| Điểm thực thi công cụ | Hub + Desktop Commander/Cloud Harness MCP | Cùng Hub + MCP |
| Giám sát | Lượt chat/đang chờ xác minh, MCP, kết quả | Ghi chú model, lượt API, MCP, kết quả, token API nếu endpoint trả |
| Chi phí | Hạn mức gói ChatGPT web | Phí/hạn mức của gateway, tách biệt khỏi ChatGPT web |

## Cài bản cập nhật trên Windows

1. Chạy `STOP-CHATMCP-HUB.cmd`, chờ dừng.
2. Giải nén ZIP vào thư mục cha `F:\Personal_Project\Vin\ChatMCP`, chọn **ghi đè file** trong `CHATMCP-HUB`; không xóa các thư mục `.generated`, workspace, hoặc nguồn dự án.
3. Trong `edge://extensions` hoặc `chrome://extensions`, **Reload ChatMCP Hub Companion 1.3.7**. Tắt bản Companion trùng lặp nếu có.
4. Chạy `START-CHATMCP-HUB.cmd`, mở `http://127.0.0.1:3007`.
5. Chọn workspace và chờ dịch vụ MCP sẵn sàng.

## Chế độ 1 — ChatGPT Web

Chọn `ChatGPT Web · Browser Companion`. Ghép Companion bằng mã 8 chữ số một lần nếu chưa ghép. Đăng nhập ChatGPT trên Edge/Chrome, chọn model như bình thường. Nhập yêu cầu trên dashboard, giữ tab riêng của tác vụ và trình duyệt mở. Đây là luồng trước đây với cơ chế chờ mạng và tự đối chiếu lượt khi có thể; không lấy reasoning nội bộ từ ChatGPT.

## Chế độ 2 — API Gateway

Chọn `API Gateway · Trực tiếp`. Mở `Thiết lập API Gateway`, nhập:

- **Giao thức** `Google Gemini generateContent` hoặc `OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions`.
- **API Base URL** của gateway. Ví dụ minh họa cho Gemini chính thức: `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com`. Gateway riêng: `https://your-gateway.example`.
- **Model** mà *gateway* thực sự cung cấp, ví dụ `gemini-3.8-flash` nếu có quyền dùng model đó.
- **API Key** của bạn (ô password). KHÔNG ghi key vào URL, prompt, mã nguồn, README, lệnh terminal, log hoặc tin nhắn.
- Tùy chọn **Windows DPAPI**: nếu bật, key lưu ở `cloud-harness-mcp\deploy\.generated\chatmcp-hub\gateway\gateway-key.dpapi`, mã hóa ràng buộc tài khoản Windows hiện tại. Nếu không bật, key chỉ nằm trong bộ nhớ tiến trình; thoát Hub phải nhập lại (hoặc cấu hình lại qua env).

Nhấn **Lưu kết nối API**, sau đó (nếu muốn) **Test API (có thể tính phí)**. Chỉ khi chọn chế độ API thì Hub mới gọi gateway bằng key. Đổi chế độ/kết nối bị khóa trong lúc tác vụ đang chạy. **Xóa API key** xóa bản đã lưu và key trong phiên, không thể xóa biến môi trường Windows do người dùng tự đặt.

Mặc định, Gemini gọi `BASE/v1beta/models/MODEL:generateContent` với `x-goog-api-key`; OpenAI-compatible gọi `BASE/v1/chat/completions` với `Authorization: Bearer`. Nếu gateway riêng có đường dẫn/header khác, mở **Gateway tùy chỉnh** và điền **Endpoint path** như `/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent` và chọn kiểu header. Đường dẫn này là absolute path tính từ root hostname, không phải URL bên ngoài. Hub không tự dò đoán chuẩn của gateway.

Nếu sử dụng biến môi trường, Hub có thể đọc `GOOGLE_API_BASE_URL`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_MODEL`. Không để key trong lệnh PowerShell hiển thị ở lịch sử. Key đã chia sẻ công khai cần được **thu hồi/rotate** trước khi sử dụng.

API mode cần một gateway hỗ trợ **tool/function calling**, không chỉ trả lời văn bản. Model dùng bốn công cụ router (`mcp_catalog`, `mcp_describe`, `mcp_call`, `mcp_capabilities`) để gọi đầy đủ công cụ MCP từ danh mục hiện có. Gemini 3.x: adapter giữ nguyên `thoughtSignature` trong lịch sử đang chạy để xử lý các lượt tool. Các phần suy luận bí mật không được trình bày trong dashboard hay bản báo cáo. Hiện API adapter chủ yếu hỗ trợ văn bản và tool calling; không hứa xử lý hình/âm thanh từ mọi MCP tool.

**Cảnh báo dữ liệu:** API mode gửi yêu cầu, một phần nội dung file/kết quả công cụ trong task cho **gateway do bạn chọn** để model xử lý. Chỉ dùng gateway mà bạn tin cậy. Các thao tác local và Cloud Harness chạy dưới quyền kết nối MCP; thư mục chọn trong UI **không phải sandbox hệ điều hành**. Công cụ có khả năng sửa/xóa file thật, kiểm tra lệnh trước các bước nhạy cảm.

## Theo dõi tác vụ

- **Đang làm gì**: trạng thái công việc mới nhất, model/công cụ đang xử lý.
- **Luồng Agent**: danh sách sự kiện theo thời gian (mục tiêu/ghi chú công khai → gọi MCP → kết quả/ lỗi → tiếp tục → báo cáo).
- **Lượt model, số MCP, usage**: giữ đầy đủ bản ghi trong thư mục task của Hub. Dashboard hiển thị thống kê và các sự kiện gần nhất.
- **Báo cáo**: file tải xuống chứa kết quả thực được ghi lại. Trạng thái `completed` nghĩa là model đã gửi câu trả lời kết thúc; KHÔNG bảo đảm code đúng nếu chưa có kết quả chạy test.

Chế độ API có ngân sách mặc định **300 lượt / 120 phút** trong dashboard, điều chỉnh từ 1–1000 lượt và 1–240 phút. Đây là giới hạn an toàn nhằm tránh API tính phí không giới hạn hoặc vòng lặp vô hạn, không phải hạn mức tài khoản.

**Mạng LAN chập chờn:** Web mode tiếp tục dùng cơ chế xác minh/khôi phục an toàn cũ. API mode chờ mạng rồi thử lại **yêu cầu model** nếu mất kết nối transport; yêu cầu cũ có thể vẫn bị tính phí. Hub không tự thực hiện lại MCP mutation đã gửi mà chưa có kết quả chắc chắn. Cần giữ tiến trình Hub chạy; sau khi đóng/restart giữa nhiệm vụ, phần công việc đang dở không được tự replay.

## Giới hạn của bản này

Đây là bản **agent task/workflow dashboard**, chưa phải bản sao đầy đủ của Codex Desktop, Antigravity hoặc Claude Desktop: chưa có thread chat follow-up tự động nhiều lần vào cùng phiên, bảng diff editor hay bộ phân quyền/approval nâng cao trong UI. Không thể truy xuất `chain-of-thought` nội bộ của ChatGPT Web hoặc các model API; chỉ hiển thị các bản tóm tắt tiến độ được phép hiển thị và thao tác có bằng chứng.

## Lệnh kiểm thử phát triển

Từ thư mục gốc của Hub, cần Node 22+:

```
node tests/verify-dual-mode.mjs
node tests/verify-agent-http.mjs
node tests/verify-network-recovery.mjs
node tests/verify-send-cycle.mjs
```

Các test mới dùng gateway và MCP giả lập; **không dùng API key thật, không tốn API và không sửa workspace Windows**. Cần chạy test tích hợp Windows/Edge/gateway thật riêng trên máy của người dùng trước khi tuyên bố tương thích với một custom gateway.
