- **Lượt model, số MCP, usage**: giữ đầy đủ bản ghi trong thư mục task của Hub. Dashboard hiển thị thống kê và các sự kiện gần nhất.
- **Báo cáo**: file tải xuống chứa kết quả thực được ghi lại. Trạng thái `completed` nghĩa là model đã gửi câu trả lời kết thúc; KHÔNG bảo đảm code đúng nếu chưa có kết quả chạy test.

Chế độ API có ngân sách mặc định **300 lượt / 120 phút** trong dashboard, điều chỉnh từ 1–1000 lượt và 1–240 phút. Đây là giới hạn an toàn nhằm tránh API tính phí không giới hạn hoặc vòng lặp vô hạn, không phải hạn mức tài khoản.

**Mạng LAN chập chờn:** Web mode tiếp tục dùng cơ chế xác minh/khôi phục an toàn cũ. API mode chờ mạng rồi thử lại **yêu cầu model** nếu mất kết nối transport; yêu cầu cũ có thể vẫn bị tính phí. Hub không tự thực hiện lại MCP mutation đã gửi mà chưa có kết quả chắc chắn. Cần giữ tiến trình Hub chạy; sau khi đóng/restart giữa nhiệm vụ, phần công việc đang dở không được tự replay.

## Giới hạn của bản này

Đây là bản **agent task/workflow dashboard**, chưa phải bản sao đầy đủ của Codex Desktop, Antigravity hoặc Claude Desktop: chưa có thread chat follow-up tự động nhiều lần vào cùng phiên, bảng diff editor hay bộ phân quyền/approval nâng cao trong UI. Không thể truy xuất `chain-of-thought` nội bộ của ChatGPT Web hoặc các model API; chỉ hiển thị các bản tóm tắt tiến độ được phép hiển thị và thao tác có bằng chứng.

## Lệnh kiểm thử phát triển

Từ thư mục gốc của Hub, cần Node 22+:

```
node tests/verify-dual-mode.mjs
node tests/verify-agent-http.mjs
node tests/verify-network-recovery.mjs
node tests/verify-send-cycle.mjs
```

Các test mới dùng gateway và MCP giả lập; **không dùng API key thật, không tốn API và không sửa workspace Windows**. Cần chạy test tích hợp Windows/Edge/gateway thật riêng trên máy của người dùng trước khi tuyên bố tương thích với một custom gateway.

CHATMCP HUB 1.1.6 / COMPANION 1.3.6 — TỰ TIẾP TỤC KHI MẠNG LAN MẤT

KHI MẠNG MẤT:
  * Không hủy nhiệm vụ và không bấm Gửi thủ công vào tab ChatGPT của Hub.
  * Giữ Hub ở localhost:3007, Edge/Chrome và tab ChatGPT của tác vụ đang mở.
  * Popup Companion và dashboard hiển thị trạng thái "Đang chờ mạng" hoặc
    "đang xác minh lượt đã gửi". Extension tự kiểm tra lại sau khoảng 3–30s.
  * Khi mạng quay lại, Companion đọc đúng tin nhắn/câu trả lời của lượt cũ
    (task + turn + nonce). Nếu chứng minh được, nó tự tiếp tục công việc.
  * Nếu mạng mất TRƯỚC click Gửi và extension nhận được kết quả chắc chắn
    chưa click, extension sẽ click LẦN ĐẦU sau khi tab sẵn sàng.

ĐỂ TRÁNH CHẠY TRÙNG LỆNH GHI/XÓA:
  * Nếu mất xác nhận sau click Gửi, extension KHÔNG bấm Gửi lần hai.
    Nó chỉ đọc tab hiện tại (reconciling) cho đến khi có bằng chứng.
  * Nếu không còn bằng chứng đúng lượt (ví dụ ChatGPT không lưu/hiện tin),
    việc tự tiếp tục có thể cần người dùng kiểm tra. Không đoán rằng đã gửi.
  * Nếu mất mạng NGAY TRONG lời gọi MCP, thao tác có thể đã chạy; Hub
    KHÔNG tự chạy lại tool ghi/xóa khi kết quả chưa rõ.
  * Không hỗ trợ tiếp tục tự động qua lần Hub Windows dừng/khởi động lại,
    hoặc trên task đã đánh dấu failed từ bản cũ.

CÀI BẢN MỚI:
  1) Đóng hoặc hủy task cũ đã lỗi. Dừng Hub bằng STOP-CHATMCP-HUB.cmd.
  2) Giải nén bản mới vào thư mục CHATMCP-HUB cũ và ghi đè file.
  3) Edge: edge://extensions -> Reload ChatMCP Hub Companion (1.3.6).
  4) Chạy START-CHATMCP-HUB.cmd. Tạo TASK MỚI.
  5) Với bài lab đã từng chạy, yêu cầu ChatGPT kiểm tra git status,
     nội dung đã sửa và log test trước khi tiếp tục, không lặp lại thao tác.

Đã thử tự động bằng mô phỏng Node/DOM/HTTP; chưa thử với Edge trên máy bạn.

before.CHATMCP-HUB/README.md:
# DatGold Hub — local runtime

Đây là Hub nền của [DatGold Studio](../README.md), chạy dưới tài khoản người dùng và chỉ phục vụ loopback (127.0.0.1). Các kết nối tới API model/GitHub là **outbound** theo tính năng được sử dụng, không phải public hosting.

## Chạy trên Windows

~~~powershell
.\START-CHATMCP-HUB.cmd -ProjectPath 'C:\Projects\Demo'
~~~

Có thể dùng backend local duy nhất; các flag -RepoRoot, -Backend mcp và CHATMCP_PUBLIC=1 đã bị loại bỏ.

## Các thành phần

- lib/manager.mjs: trạng thái Hub, workspace, local catalog và permission-gated tool sessions.
- lib/agent.mjs và lib/gateway-provider.mjs: vòng lặp coding agent và model providers.
- lib/studio-workspace.mjs, lib/local-tools.mjs, lib/git-runner.mjs: Git, file operations, checks, checkpoint.
- lib/coding-orchestrator.mjs và lib/studio-delegates.mjs: worktree coding agents và read-only DAG.
- lib/skill-registry.mjs và lib/plugins.mjs: pinned GitHub skills và import tài nguyên.
- extension/: browser companion tự chọn của người dùng, không phải Cloud Harness proxy.

## An toàn

Hub chỉ listen 127.0.0.1; mọi yêu cầu API (kể cả đọc và luồng sự kiện) phải mang bí mật theo từng lần khởi động (`Authorization: Bearer`), ghi trong `run/hub-session.json` của thư mục dữ liệu và chỉ tài khoản Windows hiện tại đọc được. Host, Origin, CSRF vẫn được kiểm tra thêm. Ranh giới này chặn tài khoản Windows khác, tiến trình sandbox và trang web trong trình duyệt; nó KHÔNG chặn mã độc chạy dưới cùng tài khoản của bạn. PermissionGate bảo vệ tools; worktree không cung cấp cách ly VM/OS. Không mở Hub trực tiếp ra Internet.

## Test

~~~powershell
node tests/run-all.mjs
~~~

Xem [README gốc](../README.md), [SECURITY](../SECURITY.md) và [Windows Setup](../docs/WINDOWS-SETUP.md).

# CI health

Two numbers decide whether CI can be trusted as evidence: **how many runs one push costs** and **how often CI fails on `main`**. This page says how the workflows are triggered, how that was checked without GitHub, how `scripts/ci-health.mjs` measures both numbers, and what the numbers were before the change. Gate G0 of the roadmap asks for: no duplicate run per push, and a failure share of the completed runs on `main` of at most 15%.

## Triggers after this change

| Workflow | Starts on | Skipped for | Concurrency group |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ci.yml` (CI) | `pull_request`; `push` to `main` only; `workflow_dispatch` | documentation-only changes (see below) | `ci-<PR number>`, or `ci-<ref>` on `main`; only pull request runs are cancelled by a newer push |
| `docs-gates.yml` (Documentation gates) | the same events, only when a changed path is a documentation path | any change that touches no documentation path | `docs-gates-<PR number or ref>` |
| `dco.yml` | `pull_request` (opened, reopened, synchronize, edited) | nothing | `dco-<PR number>` |
| `browser-companion-regression.yml` | `pull_request` and `push` to `main`, only for the Companion paths it lists; `workflow_dispatch` | other changes | `browser-companion-<PR number or ref>` |
| `browser-companion-package.yml` | the same, for the extension and its packaging scripts | other changes | `companion-zip-<PR number or ref>` |
| `publish-v*.yml` | push to `main` (12 files) or completion of CI on `main` (6 files); each job is guarded by a condition on the commit | nothing at the trigger | per commit |

What was wrong: `ci.yml` ran on `push` for `main` and for `dev/**`, `fix/**`, `feat/**`, `refactor/**` **and** on `pull_request`, so every push to a branch with a pull request started it twice. `browser-companion-regression.yml` and `browser-companion-package.yml` each pinned one feature branch in `push` with the same effect. `phase1-component-tests.yml` was pinned to a branch that no longer exists; it is deleted, and the suites it ran are part of `node tests/run-all.mjs` in `ci.yml`. A branch **without** a pull request is no longer built on push; open the pull request, or start `ci.yml` by hand (`workflow_dispatch`).

### Why documentation-only changes skip `ci.yml` but not every check

`ci.yml` ignores `*.md` (top level), `docs/**`, `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, `HUONG-DAN.txt` and `VALIDATION.txt`. Five suites read exactly those files: `verify-docs`, `verify-trust-labels`, `verify-notices`, `verify-threat-model` and, from the claims work, `verify-claims-map`. A bare `paths-ignore` would have let a README, threat model or claims-map change merge without them. `docs-gates.yml` therefore starts under the opposite condition (its `paths` list **is** the `paths-ignore` list of `ci.yml`; `tests/verify-ci-triggers.mjs` fails when the two differ) and runs those suites in about a minute. A change that touches both documentation and code runs both workflows. Files outside the list, for example `CHATMCP-HUB/tests/requirements-e2e.txt`, `CHATMCP-HUB/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` or `CHATMCP-HUB/README.md`, still start `ci.yml`.

If branch protection makes jobs of `ci.yml` **required** status checks, a documentation-only pull request leaves them "Pending" because the workflow never starts. In that case require the check `Documentation suites` for documentation changes through a ruleset that matches the same paths, or do not require path-dependent checks; no setting of the workflow files can fix this. Whether branch protection is configured is not visible from the repository.

## How "one run per push" was checked without GitHub

`tests/verify-ci-triggers.mjs` reads the real workflow files with a small model of GitHub's trigger rules (`tests/fixtures/workflow-triggers.mjs`: branch, tag and path filters with `*`, `**` and `!`, the default activity types of `pull_request`, the rule that `paths-ignore` skips a run only when every changed file matches, and the concurrency group with its expressions). It replays the events GitHub sends for one pushed commit, and for each of the 23 workflow files asserts at most one run:

- a push to a branch that has an open pull request: the `push` event and the `pull_request` "synchronize" event (nine branch names, including the two that used to be pinned);
- a code change, a documentation-only change and a mixed change;
- a merge to `main`, a push to a branch without a pull request, a tag, a manual start.

The same replay on the v3.9.0 trigger block (embedded in the test) gives **two** runs for `feat/**`, `fix/**`, `dev/**` and `refactor/**`; that is the negative control. Seven defects put into in-memory copies of the current files (an old glob back, no branch filter, a pinned branch, a documentation path lost from `docs-gates.yml`, the old concurrency group, cancelled `main` runs, documentation no longer ignored) are each detected.

**Not shown by this:** that GitHub agrees with the model. The first pull requests after the change are the proof; measure them with `ci-health.mjs --since <date of the merge>`. The model also does not cover required checks, forks or `workflow_run`.

## `scripts/ci-health.mjs`

```bash
node scripts/ci-health.mjs --repo pddczpl/ChatMCP --workflow CI
node scripts/ci-health.mjs --repo pddczpl/ChatMCP --since 2026-11-01 --json
node scripts/ci-health.mjs --fixture CHATMCP-HUB/tests/fixtures/ci-health/gh-output.json
```

It needs the GitHub CLI (`gh`, logged in) and only reads: the allow-list is `gh run list` and `gh pr list`, enforced before a process starts, and `tests/verify-ci-health.mjs` checks that no mutating verb can be built. `--fixture` replays a saved `{"runs": [...], "pulls": [...]}` file (the raw output of those two commands), which is how the arithmetic is tested offline.

Definitions, fixed in the script and repeated in its output:

- **window**: the N most recent runs of the workflow on `main` (pull request runs excluded), newest first, whatever their status; N is 50 and 100. Fewer runs than N is reported ("only 26 runs exist"), never padded.
- **completed**: status `completed`; queued and in-progress runs are counted apart.
- **failure**: conclusion `failure`, `timed_out` or `startup_failure`.
- **failure share** = failures ÷ (successes + failures). Cancelled, skipped, neutral and stale runs say nothing about the code and are reported on their own. The share of all completed runs (failures ÷ completed) is printed beside it, because the two differ a lot when many runs were cancelled (below). The gate text says "completed runs"; which of the two is meant is the owner's call, and the stricter one is the default.
- **runs per merged PR**: runs of the workflow whose head branch is the pull request's branch and that started between its creation and its merge, any event. A pull request with no run in the fetched history is "no data", not "zero runs", and stays out of the mean.
- **built twice**: two runs of the same workflow for the same commit (a `push` and a `pull_request` run, in practice).
- A re-run keeps its run id, so a failure turned green by a re-run shows as success; the number of re-run runs is printed.

Exit code: 0 when every limit holds (`--max-failure-share`, default 0.15; `--max-duplicated-commits`, default 0), 1 when one is exceeded, 2 for a usage or `gh` error, 3 when there is nothing to judge.

## Baseline before the change (read with `gh` on 2026-10-19)

| | Last 50 runs of CI on `main` | Last 100 |
|---|---|---|
| success / failure / cancelled | 11 / 2 / **37** | 37 / 7 / **56** |
| failure share (failures ÷ success+failure) | 15.4% (2 of 13) | 15.9% (7 of 44) |
| failure share of all completed runs | 4.0% | 7.0% |

- More than half of the recent runs on `main` were **cancelled**, because the old `cancel-in-progress: true` also applied to `main`: a newer push cancelled the run of the previous commit, so a red commit could be replaced before anyone saw it. For all 56 cancelled runs among the last 100, a newer run on `main` had started before the cancelled one ended (checked on the same data). Only pull request runs are cancelled now. The failure share rests on 13 and 44 decided runs, a small sample; a few failures move it by several points.
- Of the 30 most recent merged pull requests, 16 still have runs in the history. They cost **16.2 runs each**, and in 10 of them the same workflow built 112 commits twice (`push` + `pull_request`). After the change this number must be 0: `ci-health.mjs --since <merge date of the first pull request>`.

## Why the failure share was about 24% (read with `gh` on 2026-10-20, task bc-14)

The 1,000 most recent runs of `CI` (all events, 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-19) contain **62 failed, 198 successful and 740 cancelled** runs: 62 of the 260 decided runs, **23.8%**. On `main` alone (129 runs in the same window): 55 success, 15 failure, 59 cancelled, so 15 of 70 (**21.4%**); since 2026-10-17 two failures of 17 decided runs. The window is the one in which the audit's phases landed, so most failures are branch work meeting the checks, not a flaky machine.

How it was measured, so that it can be repeated: `gh run list --workflow CI --limit 1000 --json ...` for the runs, then `gh run view <id> --json jobs` and `gh run view <id> --log-failed` for each of the 62 failed ones. The suite names are the `FAIL verify-*.mjs` lines `run-all.mjs` prints; a suite that failed in all four jobs of a run is a change that broke it, one that failed only in the two Windows (or the two Linux) jobs depends on the OS, one that failed in a single job of four depends on timing or load.

## A race the study could not see: two `git worktree add` at once (read with `gh` on 2026-10-25)

`verify-subagent-notices` (section D5: a workflow of two review agents and a verifier) failed once on `windows-latest` in a `pwsh` run of the whole regression (run 40163727428). It prints the whole tail now (12,000 characters), and the assertions about agents say what the Hub recorded for each.

The cause was shown on the runner by running the suite on its own, as `run-all` starts it, in a loop (a throwaway workflow on a `pddczpl/tmp-*` branch, run 40165632854): 90 runs one at a time without a failure, 120 runs four at a time with one. Its output holds the Hub's own record of the agents:

```
Security: uncertain (Git worktree creation failed: Preparing worktree (new branch 'chatmcp/chat/486ce72d-382')
  fatal: failed to read .git/worktrees/worktree7/commondir: No error) · Correctness: completed · Independent verifier: blocked (A dependency has not completed successfully.)
```

The assertion was right and the Hub had a defect. `ConcurrentApiAgent` starts the agents of a phase together and ran `git worktree add` for all of them on the same repository at the same moment. Git makes the folder under `.git/worktrees` before the files in it, and a second `git worktree add` that looks at the folder in between dies reading a `commondir` that is still empty. The Hub marks that agent `uncertain` (its worktree may be half made) and the agents waiting for it `blocked`, as designed. The notices, the 50 ms polling of the test and the order of the phases had nothing to do with it.

| What was run (`windows-latest`, Node 24, `shell: pwsh`; "Git alone" has no Hub code) | Result |
|---|---|
| Git alone: 4 `git worktree add` started together, 1,015 rounds (ubuntu 400, `windows-latest` 500, a Windows 11 machine 115) | 4 rounds failed, each with the message above ("No error" on Windows, "Success" on Linux); started one at a time: 0 of 1,015 |
| The Hub before the fix (main `a45325b`): 8 agents at once, 24 worktrees already in the repository, 160 rounds | `git worktree add` overlapped in 160 of 160 rounds (up to 8 at once); an agent ended `uncertain` in 3 rounds (4 of 1,280 agents), each time with that message |
| The Hub with the fix, the same 160 rounds | overlapped in 0 rounds (never more than one); 1,280 of 1,280 agents completed |

The failure is rare (3 rounds in 160 above, 1 run in 120 of the suite), so the count of failures alone would not prove the fix. What shows it is the overlap, which is counted in every round and which the fix removes, together with the message. `ConcurrentApiAgent#worktreeTurn` now gives each repository a line of turns: an agent takes its turn after the approval step and keeps it for the crash marker and the `git worktree add`. The price is that the checkouts of agents that start together are made one after the other (8 agents of a tiny repository: about 0.7 s before, 1.5 s after, on a developer machine). `verify-subagent-notices` D8 counts the calls that run at the same moment, D9 covers a stop while an agent waits and a Git call that throws, and D10 that the question to the person (Review mode) comes before the turn. The coding orchestrator already set up its workers one at a time for the same reason. Still unprotected, and left alone: `gitRefs` (`git worktree list`), the studio tool `worktrees_create` and the coding orchestrator's own `git worktree add` calls (one at a time among themselves, but with no turn shared with the pool's), which can meet the same Git failure while the pool makes a worktree.

## Retry, `FLAKY`, and the streak gate

`node tests/run-all.mjs --retry-failed-once` (used by `ci.yml`) runs a suite that **failed or timed out** a second time, once.

| First attempt | Second attempt | Result | Counts as |
|---|---|---|---|
| passes | not run | `PASS` | pass |
| fails or times out | passes | **`FLAKY`** | `summary.flaky`, never `summary.pass` |
| fails or times out | fails or times out | `FAIL` / `TIMEOUT` ("failed twice") | fail / timeout |
| fails or times out | skips | `FAIL` ("a skip never rescues a failure") | fail |

A `FLAKY` entry in `summary.json` carries both attempts with their exit codes, notes and **the output of the attempt that failed**; the console prints that output under the table line, and GitHub Actions gets a `::warning title=FLAKY suite` annotation and a line in the step summary. One `FLAKY` suite does not make the run red (a retry exists for the rare accident); `--fail-on-flaky` makes it red where nothing should need a retry.

The same suite passing only on retry in run after run is a defect, not an accident. `scripts/ci-flaky-gate.mjs` (job `flaky-gate` of `ci.yml`, on pushes to `main` only, after `hub-tests` succeeded) adds up the `FLAKY` counts of the `hub-test-summary-*` artifacts of this run and of the previous ones and **fails when this run and the two runs of `main` before it each had one**. Definitions: a *flaky run* has more than 0 `FLAKY` suites in its summaries (a summary from before the retry existed counts 0); a run with no readable summary is *unknown* and ends a streak, because the gate never fails on something it did not see; the history is the previous completed `push` runs of `CI` on `main` that ended in success or failure, newest first. The script only reads GitHub (`gh run list`, `gh run download`; the artifacts go to a temporary folder). `tests/verify-test-runner.mjs` tests the retry rules, the decision function and the command line against fixture folders; mutating any of them (FLAKY reported as PASS, a skip rescuing a failure, an off-by-one streak, unknown counted as flaky) fails it.

## G1-8, and what it cannot be

Gate G1-8 asks for a failure share of the completed runs on `main` of at most 10% **and** four consecutive weekly releases. The owner has decided there is no release until the whole roadmap is done, so the second half cannot be met as written. The evidence that stands in for it, once the first half holds: four consecutive weeks in which the completed `CI` runs on `main` have a failure share of at most 10% (`node scripts/ci-health.mjs --since <date>` reports it), with no streak of `FLAKY` runs (`flaky-gate` green on every push), plus a dry run of the release pipeline once one exists. The two must be read together: a retry turns a flaky suite into a pass as far as the failure share goes, so a share of at most 10% only means something next to the number of `FLAKY` suites per run (every summary has it), and a month of green runs with a FLAKY suite in each of them is not the evidence. The share on `main` since 2026-10-17 is 2 of 17 (11.8%), too few runs to claim anything. One exception to "no release": on 2026-10-25 the owner asked for a single test build, 3.10.0, published as a pre-release. If its publication succeeds it is the dry run of the release pipeline that this paragraph asks for; it is not one of the four weekly releases and the rule for the roadmap's own releases stands. A second test build, 3.10.1, with the fixes and notices made after 3.10.0, was prepared on the same day on the same terms (a pre-release, never the latest release).

## Not verified here, and open

- The first real run of `docs-gates.yml`, of the changed concurrency expressions, and of the claims job: nothing here can start a GitHub run. They are checked by the trigger model and by running the same commands locally (`verify-docs`, `verify-trust-labels`, `verify-notices`, `verify-threat-model`).
- `publish-v*.yml`: 18 old release workflows remain. Twelve start on **every** push to `main` and six on every completion of CI on `main`; their jobs are guarded by a condition on the commit message and end "skipped", but each one is a run. They inflate the run count per merge on `main` (not per pull request) and hide the interesting runs in the list. Deleting those of releases that are out is the owner's decision, so it is not done here. `ci-health.mjs` counts the `CI` workflow by default for that reason.

A bare `paths-ignore` would have let a README, threat model or claims-map change merge without them. `docs-gates.yml` therefore starts under the opposite condition (its `paths` list **is** the `paths-ignore` list of `ci.yml`; `tests/verify-ci-triggers.mjs` fails when the two differ) and runs those suites in about a minute. A change that touches both documentation and code runs both workflows. Files outside the list, for example `CHATMCP-HUB/tests/requirements-e2e.txt`, `CHATMCP-HUB/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` or `CHATMCP-HUB/README.md`, still start `ci.yml`.

If branch protection makes jobs of `ci.yml` **required** status checks, a documentation-only pull request leaves them "Pending" because the workflow never starts. In that case require the check `Documentation suites` for documentation changes through a ruleset that matches the same paths, or do not require path-dependent checks; no setting of the workflow files can fix this. Whether branch protection is configured is not visible from the repository.

## How "one run per push" was checked without GitHub

`tests/verify-ci-triggers.mjs` reads the real workflow files with a small model of GitHub's trigger rules (`tests/fixtures/workflow-triggers.mjs`: branch, tag and path filters with `*`, `**` and `!`, the default activity types of `pull_request`, the rule that `paths-ignore` skips a run only when every changed file matches, and the concurrency group with its expressions). It replays the events GitHub sends for one pushed commit, and for each of the 23 workflow files asserts at most one run:

- a push to a branch that has an open pull request: the `push` event and the `pull_request` "synchronize" event (nine branch names, including the two that used to be pinned);
- a code change, a documentation-only change and a mixed change;
- a merge to `main`, a push to a branch without a pull request, a tag, a manual start.

The same replay on the v3.9.0 trigger block (embedded in the test) gives **two** runs for `feat/**`, `fix/**`, `dev/**` and `refactor/**`; that is the negative control. Seven defects put into in-memory copies of the current files (an old glob back, no branch filter, a pinned branch, a documentation path lost from `docs-gates.yml`, the old concurrency group, cancelled `main` runs, documentation no longer ignored) are each detected.

**Not shown by this:** that GitHub agrees with the model. The first pull requests after the change are the proof; measure them with `ci-health.mjs --since <date of the merge>`. The model also does not cover required checks, forks or `workflow_run`.

## `scripts/ci-health.mjs`

```bash
node scripts/ci-health.mjs --repo pddczpl/ChatMCP --workflow CI
node scripts/ci-health.mjs --repo pddczpl/ChatMCP --since 2026-11-01 --json
node scripts/ci-health.mjs --fixture CHATMCP-HUB/tests/fixtures/ci-health/gh-output.json
```

It needs the GitHub CLI (`gh`, logged in) and only reads: the allow-list is `gh run list` and `gh pr list`, enforced before a process starts, and `tests/verify-ci-health.mjs` checks that no mutating verb can be built. `--fixture` replays a saved `{"runs": [...], "pulls": [...]}` file (the raw output of those two commands), which is how the arithmetic is tested offline.

Definitions, fixed in the script and repeated in its output:

- **window**: the N most recent runs of the workflow on `main` (pull request runs excluded), newest first, whatever their status; N is 50 and 100. Fewer runs than N is reported ("only 26 runs exist"), never padded.
- **completed**: status `completed`; queued and in-progress runs are counted apart.
- **failure**: conclusion `failure`, `timed_out` or `startup_failure`.
- **failure share** = failures ÷ (successes + failures). Cancelled, skipped, neutral and stale runs say nothing about the code and are reported on their own. The share of all completed runs (failures ÷ completed) is printed beside it, because the two differ a lot when many runs were cancelled (below). The gate text says "completed runs"; which of the two is meant is the owner's call, and the stricter one is the default.
- **runs per merged PR**: runs of the workflow whose head branch is the pull request's branch and that started between its creation and its merge, any event. A pull request with no run in the fetched history is "no data", not "zero runs", and stays out of the mean.
- **built twice**: two runs of the same workflow for the same commit (a `push` and a `pull_request` run, in practice).
- A re-run keeps its run id, so a failure turned green by a re-run shows as success; the number of re-run runs is printed.

Exit code: 0 when every limit holds (`--max-failure-share`, default 0.15; `--max-duplicated-commits`, default 0), 1 when one is exceeded, 2 for a usage or `gh` error, 3 when there is nothing to judge.

## Baseline before the change (read with `gh` on 2026-10-19)

| | Last 50 runs of CI on `main` | Last 100 |
|---|---|---|
| success / failure / cancelled | 11 / 2 / **37** | 37 / 7 / **56** |
| failure share (failures ÷ success+failure) | 15.4% (2 of 13) | 15.9% (7 of 44) |
| failure share of all completed runs | 4.0% | 7.0% |

- More than half of the recent runs on `main` were **cancelled**, because the old `cancel-in-progress: true` also applied to `main`: a newer push cancelled the run of the previous commit, so a red commit could be replaced before anyone saw it. For all 56 cancelled runs among the last 100, a newer run on `main` had started before the cancelled one ended (checked on the same data). Only pull request runs are cancelled now. The failure share rests on 13 and 44 decided runs, a small sample; a few failures move it by several points.
- Of the 30 most recent merged pull requests, 16 still have runs in the history. They cost **16.2 runs each**, and in 10 of them the same workflow built 112 commits twice (`push` + `pull_request`). After the change this number must be 0: `ci-health.mjs --since <merge date of the first pull request>`.

## Why the failure share was about 24% (read with `gh` on 2026-10-20, task bc-14)

The 1,000 most recent runs of `CI` (all events, 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-19) contain **62 failed, 198 successful and 740 cancelled** runs: 62 of the 260 decided runs, **23.8%**. On `main` alone (129 runs in the same window): 55 success, 15 failure, 59 cancelled, so 15 of 70 (**21.4%**); since 2026-10-17 two failures of 17 decided runs. The window is the one in which the audit's phases landed, so most failures are branch work meeting the checks, not a flaky machine.

How it was measured, so that it can be repeated: `gh run list --workflow CI --limit 1000 --json ...` for the runs, then `gh run view <id> --json jobs` and `gh run view <id> --log-failed` for each of the 62 failed ones. ## A race the study could not see: two `git worktree add` at once (read with `gh` on 2026-10-25)

`verify-subagent-notices` (section D5: a workflow of two review agents and a verifier) failed once on `windows-latest` in a `pwsh` run of the whole regression (run 40163727428). It passed in the four Hub jobs of the pull request, in the first publish run of v3.10.0 and 20 of 20 times on a developer machine, and the publish workflows run without `--retry-failed-once`, so one such failure stops a release. `run-all.mjs` printed the last 25 lines of the failure, which ended inside the "expected" dump, so the rows the test had read were not in the log. It prints the whole tail now (12,000 characters), and the assertions about agents say what the Hub recorded for each.

The cause was shown on the runner by running the suite on its own, as `run-all` starts it, in a loop (a throwaway workflow on a `pddczpl/tmp-*` branch, run 40165632854): 90 runs one at a time without a failure, 120 runs four at a time with one. Its output holds the Hub's own record of the agents:

```
Security: uncertain (Git worktree creation failed: Preparing worktree (new branch 'chatmcp/chat/486ce72d-382')
  fatal: failed to read .git/worktrees/worktree7/commondir: No error) · Correctness: completed · Independent verifier: blocked (A dependency has not completed successfully.)
```

The assertion was right and the Hub had a defect. `ConcurrentApiAgent` starts the agents of a phase together and ran `git worktree add` for all of them on the same repository at the same moment. Git makes the folder under `.git/worktrees` before the files in it, and a second `git worktree add` that looks at the folder in between dies reading a `commondir` that is still empty. The Hub marks that agent `uncertain` (its worktree may be half made) and the agents waiting for it `blocked`, as designed. The notices, the 50 ms polling of the test and the order of the phases had nothing to do with it.

| What was run (`windows-latest`, Node 24, `shell: pwsh`; "Git alone" has no Hub code) | Result |
|---|---|
| Git alone: 4 `git worktree add` started together, 1,015 rounds (ubuntu 400, `windows-latest` 500, a Windows 11 machine 115) | 4 rounds failed, each with the message above ("No error" on Windows, "Success" on Linux); started one at a time: 0 of 1,015 |
| The Hub before the fix (main `a45325b`): 8 agents at once, 24 worktrees already in the repository, 160 rounds | `git worktree add` overlapped in 160 of 160 rounds (up to 8 at once); an agent ended `uncertain` in 3 rounds (4 of 1,280 agents), each time with that message |
| The Hub with the fix, the same 160 rounds | overlapped in 0 rounds (never more than one); 1,280 of 1,280 agents completed |

The failure is rare (3 rounds in 160 above, 1 run in 120 of the suite), so the count of failures alone would not prove the fix. What shows it is the overlap, which is counted in every round and which the fix removes, together with the message. `ConcurrentApiAgent#worktreeTurn` now gives each repository a line of turns: an agent takes its turn after the approval step and keeps it for the crash marker and the `git worktree add`. The price is that the checkouts of agents that start together are made one after the other (8 agents of a tiny repository: about 0.7 s before, 1.5 s after, on a developer machine). `verify-subagent-notices` D8 counts the calls that run at the same moment, D9 covers a stop while an agent waits and a Git call that throws, and D10 that the question to the person (Review mode) comes before the turn. The coding orchestrator already set up its workers one at a time for the same reason. Still unprotected, and left alone: `gitRefs` (`git worktree list`), the studio tool `worktrees_create` and the coding orchestrator's own `git worktree add` calls (one at a time among themselves, but with no turn shared with the pool's), which can meet the same Git failure while the pool makes a worktree.

## Retry, `FLAKY`, and the streak gate

`node tests/run-all.mjs --retry-failed-once` (used by `ci.yml`) runs a suite that **failed or timed out** a second time, once.

| First attempt | Second attempt | Result | Counts as |
|---|---|---|---|
| passes | not run | `PASS` | pass |
| fails or times out | passes | **`FLAKY`** | `summary.flaky`, never `summary.pass` |
| fails or times out | fails or times out | `FAIL` / `TIMEOUT` ("failed twice") | fail / timeout |
| fails or times out | skips | `FAIL` ("a skip never rescues a failure") | fail |

A `FLAKY` entry in `summary.json` carries both attempts with their exit codes, notes and **the output of the attempt that failed**; the console prints that output under the table line, and GitHub Actions gets a `::warning title=FLAKY suite` annotation and a line in the step summary. One `FLAKY` suite does not make the run red (a retry exists for the rare accident); `--fail-on-flaky` makes it red where nothing should need a retry.

The same suite passing only on retry in run after run is a defect, not an accident. `scripts/ci-flaky-gate.mjs` (job `flaky-gate` of `ci.yml`, on pushes to `main` only, after `hub-tests` succeeded) adds up the `FLAKY` counts of the `hub-test-summary-*` artifacts of this run and of the previous ones and **fails when this run and the two runs of `main` before it each had one**. Definitions: a *flaky run* has more than 0 `FLAKY` suites in its summaries (a summary from before the retry existed counts 0); a run with no readable summary is *unknown* and ends a streak, because the gate never fails on something it did not see; the history is the previous completed `push` runs of `CI` on `main` that ended in success or failure, newest first. The script only reads GitHub (`gh run list`, `gh run download`; the artifacts go to a temporary folder). `tests/verify-test-runner.mjs` tests the retry rules, the decision function and the command line against fixture folders; mutating any of them (FLAKY reported as PASS, a skip rescuing a failure, an off-by-one streak, unknown counted as flaky) fails it.

## G1-8, and what it cannot be

Gate G1-8 asks for a failure share of the completed runs on `main` of at most 10% **and** four consecutive weekly releases. The owner has decided there is no release until the whole roadmap is done, so the second half cannot be met as written. The evidence that stands in for it, once the first half holds: four consecutive weeks in which the completed `CI` runs on `main` have a failure share of at most 10% (`node scripts/ci-health.mjs --since <date>` reports it), with no streak of `FLAKY` runs (`flaky-gate` green on every push), plus a dry run of the release pipeline once one exists. The two must be read together: a retry turns a flaky suite into a pass as far as the failure share goes, so a share of at most 10% only means something next to the number of `FLAKY` suites per run (every summary has it), and a month of green runs with a FLAKY suite in each of them is not the evidence. The share on `main` since 2026-10-17 is 2 of 17 (11.8%), too few runs to claim anything. One exception to "no release": on 2026-10-25 the owner asked for a single test build, 3.10.0, published as a pre-release. If its publication succeeds it is the dry run of the release pipeline that this paragraph asks for; it is not one of the four weekly releases and the rule for the roadmap's own releases stands. A second test build, 3.10.1, with the fixes and notices made after 3.10.0, was prepared on the same day on the same terms (a pre-release, never the latest release). Later the same day the owner asked for a normal release of the same line, 3.10.2, published as the latest release; it is not one of the four weekly releases either, and the rule for the roadmap's own releases stands.

## Not verified here, and open

- The first real run of `docs-gates.yml`, of the changed concurrency expressions, and of the claims job: nothing here can start a GitHub run. They are checked by the trigger model and by running the same commands locally (`verify-docs`, `verify-trust-labels`, `verify-notices`, `verify-threat-model`).
- `publish-v*.yml`: 18 old release workflows remain. Twelve start on **every** push to `main` and six on every completion of CI on `main`; their jobs are guarded by a condition on the commit message and end "skipped", but each one is a run. They inflate the run count per merge on `main` (not per pull request) and hide the interesting runs in the list. Deleting those of releases that are out is the owner's decision, so it is not done here. `ci-health.mjs` counts the `CI` workflow by default for that reason.

            git push origin "refs/tags/$TAG"

# ChatMCP Security Policy

This policy describes the current single-owner, local-first Windows product. It does not claim a security audit, fully isolated host command execution, or live-browser acceptance of every website revision.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Use GitHub's private **Report a vulnerability / Security Advisory** option for this repository if it is available. Never post API keys, tokens, private keys, exploit payloads containing secrets, or personal data in public issues. If a private reporting channel is not available, open a minimal public [issue](https://github.com/pddczpl/ChatMCP/issues) asking the maintainer to arrange a private disclosure channel. Do not disclose the vulnerability details publicly before that channel is established.

## Supported deployment boundary

ChatMCP is designed for a single local Windows account with a Hub listening on **127.0.0.1:3007**. The desktop client and the browser dashboard communicate with the loopback Hub. Public port binding, reverse-proxy publication, cloud-hosted Cloud Harness infrastructure, public multi-tenant use, and mandatory cloud accounts are not supported deployment modes.

The local HTTP interface validates Host and Origin and applies CSRF protection to mutations. Browser Companion pairing grants separately authenticated access for the user's own ChatGPT tab; it is not a public remote-control interface. Other processes running with the same Windows account must still be treated as a security concern. Loopback binding is **not** protection against malware already executing as that user.

## Permissions and execution isolation

- **Read Only:** inspect without approving file, shell, or Git mutations.
- **Review:** ask the owner to approve potentially mutating or risky operations.
- **Autonomous:** allow only operations permitted by the selected policy and the PermissionGate.
- **Full Access:** requires explicit owner activation. Operations execute using the signed-in Windows account's effective permissions. This is not OS privilege elevation, nor a promise that host commands are harmless.

Repository text, instructions in third-party skills, search results, agent replies, and tool outputs are untrusted inputs and may contain prompt injection. Path normalization, protected paths, permission checks, review tokens, checkpoints, and rollback guards reduce risk but do not make arbitrary shell commands safe. Git worktrees isolate branch checkouts, **not** host processes or filesystem permissions. Host command results must not be described as Windows Sandbox or independent attestation. Where supported, Windows Sandbox execution and sealed verification receipts have their own provenance requirements; experimental support does not prove every test runner is isolated or independently certified.

An interrupted or timed-out mutation can have uncertain effects. ChatMCP must preserve evidence and require inspection instead of blindly repeating file writes, Git operations, shell commands, or browser submissions.

## Credentials, providers, and diagnostics

Configured model API requests may transmit task instructions, selected source excerpts, tool definitions and output, images/attachments, and conversation context to the selected provider or custom gateway. **Local-first does not mean offline.** Users are responsible for selecting and trusting remote endpoints, verifying allowed sharing, and checking provider retention and charging terms. Ollama or LM Studio can operate locally when installed and configured separately.

Where stored, model credentials use the local Windows DPAPI-based secret protection mechanisms. Environment-sourced and session-only credentials have separate lifetimes. Switching credential destinations must not silently forward existing keys to an unrelated origin. Avoid entering sensitive content into model prompts or untrusted source repositories. Diagnostic exports and errors should redact known secrets, but redaction is defense in depth and not a guarantee against every accidental disclosure; inspect logs before sharing them.

Skills Hub downloads pinned repository assets and verifies content hashes; importing a skill is not permission to execute bundled scripts automatically. Upstream licensing and integrity must be reviewed independently.

## Browser Companion and desktop lifecycle

The separately installed Chrome/Edge Manifest V3 Companion pairs with the loopback Hub using a user-approved process. Its ChatGPT Web transport is constrained to supported text-based interaction and transport-specific safety checks. Pairing does not grant API quota. Browser verification on scripted pages is not equivalent to a signed-in user's live ChatGPT session. If a send outcome is uncertain, recovery must not duplicate submissions.

The native desktop enforces single-instance activation, Hub identity/version checks, and ownership-sensitive lifecycle operations. Closing the GUI preserves the running Hub; use an explicit shutdown to stop it. The installer checks owned payloads, prevents unsafe active-task upgrades, stages changes, and retains rollback markers when completion is uncertain. These controls do not provide power-loss atomicity for an entire directory or defend against an adversarial process with the same Windows privileges.

## Distribution and historic risk

Validate downloaded installers and Companion archives against the release SHA-256 files and release manifest. Verify Authenticode independently when a publisher signature is present. An unsigned installer must be described as unsigned; checksum verification only checks byte integrity relative to the published hash. Signing must precede final checksum calculation.

Older repository history may still contain retired Cloud Harness configuration or credentials. Removing files from the latest branch does **not** erase Git history or revoke a leaked secret. Rotate any potentially exposed credentials and separately decommission old servers, tokens, and deployment resources. Do not treat passing CI, successful packaging, or release checksums as a penetration test.

# Publish only the user-authorized release commit. All gates use that exact SHA.
name: Publish ChatMCP v3.8.3
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: publish-chatmcp-v3.8.3-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  browser:
    name: Real Chromium MV3 delivery gate
    if: >-
      ${{ startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'release: ChatMCP v3.8.3') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020
        with:
          node-version: '24'
      - name: Run actual extension IPC on scripted pages, without live login
        working-directory: CHATMCP-HUB/ui
        env:
          PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_FILE: ${{ runner.temp }}/companion-release-evidence/results.json
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/companion-release-evidence"
          npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
          npx playwright test e2e/companion-ipc.spec.mjs --workers=1 --reporter=line,json
      - name: Preserve browser evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
        with:
          name: ChatMCP-v3.8.3-browser-evidence
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/companion-release-evidence
          if-no-files-found: error
  windows:
    name: Build and test installed Windows upgrade
    if: >-
      ${{ startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'release: ChatMCP v3.8.3') }}
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 75
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: pwsh
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020
        with:
          node-version: '24'
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@67a3573c9a986a3f9c594539f4ab511d57bb3ce9
        with:
          dotnet-version: '10.0.x'
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Guard exact commit and all component versions
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          New-Item -ItemType Directory "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence" -Force | Out-Null
          $env:GITHUB_SHA | Set-Content "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/commit.txt" -Encoding utf8
          if ((git rev-parse HEAD).Trim() -ne $env:GITHUB_SHA) { throw 'Wrong checkout' }
          if ((git show -s --format=%s HEAD).Trim() -ne 'release: ChatMCP v3.8.3') { throw 'Wrong release commit' }
          foreach ($file in @('CHATMCP-HUB/package.json','CHATMCP-HUB/ui/package.json','CHATMCP-HUB/ui/package-lock.json')) {
            if ((Get-Content $file -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable)['version'] -ne '3.8.3') { throw "Version mismatch: $file" }
          }
          foreach ($file in @('desktop-shell/ChatMCP.csproj','installer/ChatMCP.Installer.csproj')) {
            if (-not (Get-Content $file -Raw).Contains('<Version>3.8.3</Version>')) { throw "Native version mismatch: $file" }
          }
          if ((Get-Content CHATMCP-HUB/extension/manifest.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).version -ne '1.5.2') { throw 'Companion version mismatch' }
          if (-not (Test-Path RELEASE-NOTES-v3.8.3.md)) { throw 'Missing release notes' }
      - name: Native health, ownership and transactional rollback regression
        run: |
          dotnet run --project scripts/tests/native-lifecycle/NativeLifecycle.Tests.csproj --configuration Release 2>&1 | Tee-Object "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/native-unit.log"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Native unit regression failed' }
          powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/Test-InstallerPayload.ps1
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Installer payload regression failed' }
      - name: Complete no-skip Hub regression
        run: |
          python -m pip install -r CHATMCP-HUB/tests/requirements-e2e.txt
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Dependency installation failed' }
          git config --global user.email 'ci@example.invalid'
          git config --global user.name 'ci'
          node CHATMCP-HUB/tests/run-all.mjs --no-skip all --json "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/node-summary.json" 2>&1 | Tee-Object "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/node-all.log"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Hub regression failed' }
      - name: Build fresh versioned Windows installer
        run: |
          powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/Build-Installer.ps1 2>&1 | Tee-Object "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/build.log"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Installer build failed' }
      - name: Retrieve published hash-pinned upgrade baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh release download v3.8.2 --repo $env:GITHUB_REPOSITORY --pattern ChatMCPSetup.exe --dir "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-baseline"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Baseline download failed' }
          if ((Get-FileHash "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-baseline/ChatMCPSetup.exe" -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne '75bd3085f73af083d772b675729376d2702448f8a8dc4fe94a9cd58ed80d5564') { throw 'Baseline checksum mismatch' }
      - name: Real setup upgrade, installed EXE lifecycle and uninstall
        run: |
          powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/tests/Test-NativeLifecycle.ps1 -BaselineInstaller "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-baseline/ChatMCPSetup.exe" -CandidateInstaller dist/ChatMCPSetup.exe -OutputDirectory "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/installed-lifecycle"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Installed EXE acceptance failed' }
      - name: Native WebView2 smoke and canonical Companion parity
        run: |
          node CHATMCP-HUB/ui/e2e/webview2-smoke.mjs
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'WebView2 smoke failed' }
          powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/Build-BrowserCompanion.ps1 -VerifyInstallerPayload
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Companion source/ZIP/payload parity failed' }
      - name: Verify final asset checksums and record provenance
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          $assets = @()
          foreach ($name in @('ChatMCPSetup.exe','ChatMCP-Browser-Companion.zip')) {
            $file = Join-Path dist $name
            $actual = (Get-FileHash $file -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
            $expected = ((Get-Content "$file.sha256" -Raw).Trim() -split '\s+')[0].ToLowerInvariant()
            if ($actual -ne $expected) { throw "Checksum mismatch: $name" }
            $assets += [ordered]@{ name=$name; sha256=$actual; bytes=(Get-Item $file).Length }
          }
          $native = Get-Content "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/installed-lifecycle/report.json" -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
          if ($native.result -ne 'PASS' -or $native.candidateSha256 -ne $assets[0].sha256) { throw 'Native evidence does not match the release EXE' }
          [ordered]@{ version='3.8.3'; companionVersion='1.5.2'; commit=$env:GITHUB_SHA; workflowRun=$env:GITHUB_RUN_ID; assets=$assets; signedInEdgeVerified=$false; authenticodeSigned=$false } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6 | Set-Content dist/RELEASE-MANIFEST.json -Encoding utf8
          @'
          import hashlib, json, os, re, subprocess
          from pathlib import Path

          def allowed_metadata_update(original: bytes, actual: bytes, checksum: str) -> bool:
              before = original.replace(b'\r\n', b'\n')
              after = actual.replace(b'\r\n', b'\n')
              if before == after:
                  return True
              # Exactly one existing SHA-256 in README may be replaced, and only
              # with the verified EXE's digest. No other source edit is allowed.
              if re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-f]{64}', checksum) is None:
                  return False
              for match in re.finditer(rb'(?<![0-9a-fA-F])[0-9a-fA-F]{64}(?![0-9a-fA-F])', before):
                  candidate = before[:match.start()] + checksum.encode('ascii') + before[match.end():]
                  if candidate == after:
                      return True
              return False

          # Regression checks for unchanged/CRLF and exact generated metadata;
          # unrelated edits, wrong hashes and multiple substitutions are rejected.
          sample = b'Installer checksum: ' + b'a' * 64 + b'\nOther text.\n'
          checksum = 'b' * 64
          assert allowed_metadata_update(sample, sample, checksum)
          assert allowed_metadata_update(sample, sample.replace(b'a' * 64, b'b' * 64), checksum)
          assert allowed_metadata_update(sample, sample.replace(b'\n', b'\r\n'), checksum)
          assert not allowed_metadata_update(sample, sample.replace(b'a' * 64, b'c' * 64), checksum)
          assert not allowed_metadata_update(sample, sample.replace(b'a' * 64, b'b' * 64) + b'extra', checksum)
          assert not allowed_metadata_update(sample, sample.replace(b'Other', b'Wrong'), checksum)
          assert not allowed_metadata_update(sample + sample, (sample + sample).replace(b'a' * 64, b'b' * 64), checksum)
          manifest = json.loads(Path('dist/RELEASE-MANIFEST.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig'))
          asset = next(a for a in manifest['assets'] if a['name'] == 'ChatMCPSetup.exe')
          with Path('dist/ChatMCPSetup.exe').open('rb') as stream:
              checksum = hashlib.file_digest(stream, 'sha256').hexdigest()
          assert checksum == asset['sha256'], 'Verify installer digest before metadata handling'
          original = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', 'HEAD:README.md'])
          actual = Path('README.md').read_bytes()
          assert allowed_metadata_update(original, actual, checksum), 'Unexpected README edit: refusing release'
          patch = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'diff', '--', 'README.md'])
          proof = Path(os.environ['RUNNER_TEMP']) / 'native-release-evidence'
          (proof / 'generated-readme-checksum.patch').write_bytes(patch)
          if original.replace(b'\r\n', b'\n') != actual.replace(b'\r\n', b'\n'):
              subprocess.run(['git', 'restore', '--source=HEAD', '--', 'README.md'], check=True)
          subprocess.run(['git', 'diff', '--exit-code'], check=True)
          subprocess.run(['git', 'diff', '--cached', '--exit-code'], check=True)
          print('Tracked source unchanged; verified generated README checksum recorded separately.')
          '@ | python -
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Build changed tracked source beyond verified checksum metadata' }
      - name: Upload tested release files
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
        with:
          name: ChatMCP-v3.8.3-Windows-and-Companion
          path: |
            dist/ChatMCPSetup.exe
            dist/ChatMCPSetup.exe.sha256
            dist/ChatMCP-Browser-Companion.zip
            dist/ChatMCP-Browser-Companion.zip.sha256
            dist/RELEASE-MANIFEST.json
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Preserve actual Windows evidence even on failure
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
        with:
          name: ChatMCP-v3.8.3-native-evidence
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/native-release-evidence
          if-no-files-found: error
  publish:
    name: Publish verified v3.8.3 release
    needs: [browser, windows]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: read
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      TAG: v3.8.3
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Require regular CI success on this exact release commit
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for attempt in $(seq 1 60); do
            result=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$GITHUB_SHA&event=push&per_page=100" --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.path == ".github/workflows/ci.yml")][0] | [.status // "missing", .conclusion // "none"] | @tsv')
            read -r status conclusion <<< "$result"
            if [ "$status" = completed ]; then
              test "$conclusion" = success || { echo "CI ended: $conclusion"; exit 1; }
              exit 0
            fi
            sleep 15
          done
          echo 'CI did not finish successfully before publication deadline'; exit 1
      - name: Retrieve only artifacts from this successful workflow run
        run: |
          gh run download "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --name ChatMCP-v3.8.3-Windows-and-Companion --dir dist
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib, json, os
          from pathlib import Path
          root = Path('dist')
          manifest = json.loads((root / 'RELEASE-MANIFEST.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig'))
          assert manifest['commit'] == os.environ['GITHUB_SHA']
          assert manifest['version'] == '3.8.3' and manifest['companionVersion'] == '1.5.2'
          assert {a['name'] for a in manifest['assets']} == {'ChatMCPSetup.exe', 'ChatMCP-Browser-Companion.zip'}
          for asset in manifest['assets']:
              file = root / asset['name']
              assert file.stat().st_size == asset['bytes']
              digest = hashlib.file_digest(file.open('rb'), 'sha256').hexdigest()
              assert digest == asset['sha256']
              assert digest == (root / (asset['name'] + '.sha256')).read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig').split()[0]
          print('Exact-commit release asset hashes verified again before publication.')
          PY
      - name: Publish version tag without moving existing tags and release assets
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          test "$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)" = "$GITHUB_SHA" || { echo 'main moved; refusing stale publication'; exit 1; }
          if git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            git fetch origin "refs/tags/$TAG:refs/tags/$TAG"
            test "$(git rev-list -n1 "$TAG")" = "$GITHUB_SHA" || { echo 'Tag points at another commit'; exit 1; }
          else
            git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
            git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
            git tag -a "$TAG" -m 'ChatMCP v3.8.3 - Native Lifecycle and Companion Safety' "$GITHUB_SHA"
            git push origin "refs/tags/$TAG"
          fi
          gh release create "$TAG" dist/ChatMCPSetup.exe dist/ChatMCPSetup.exe.sha256 dist/ChatMCP-Browser-Companion.zip dist/ChatMCP-Browser-Companion.zip.sha256 dist/RELEASE-MANIFEST.json --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --verify-tag --draft --title 'ChatMCP v3.8.3 - Native Lifecycle and Companion Safety' --notes-file RELEASE-NOTES-v3.8.3.md
          gh release edit "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --draft=false --latest

          foreach ($file in @('CHATMCP-HUB/package.json','CHATMCP-HUB/ui/package.json','CHATMCP-HUB/ui/package-lock.json')) {
            if ((Get-Content $file -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable)['version'] -ne '3.8.3') { throw "Version mismatch: $file" }
          }
          foreach ($file in @('desktop-shell/ChatMCP.csproj','installer/ChatMCP.Installer.csproj')) {
            if (-not (Get-Content $file -Raw).Contains('<Version>3.8.3</Version>')) { throw "Native version mismatch: $file" }
          }
          if ((Get-Content CHATMCP-HUB/extension/manifest.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).version -ne '1.5.2') { throw 'Companion version mismatch' }
          if (-not (Test-Path RELEASE-NOTES-v3.8.3.md)) { throw 'Missing release notes' }
      - name: Native health, ownership and transactional rollback regression
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p test_release_source.py -v
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Release source provenance regression failed' }
          dotnet run --project scripts/tests/native-lifecycle/NativeLifecycle.Tests.csproj --configuration Release 2>&1 | Tee-Object "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/native-unit.log"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Native unit regression failed' }
          powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/Test-InstallerPayload.ps1
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Installer payload regression failed' }
      - name: Complete no-skip Hub regression
        run: |
          python -m pip install -r CHATMCP-HUB/tests/requirements-e2e.txt
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Dependency installation failed' }
          git config --global user.email 'ci@example.invalid'
          git config --global user.name 'ci'
          node CHATMCP-HUB/tests/run-all.mjs --no-skip all --json "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/node-summary.json" 2>&1 | Tee-Object "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/node-all.log"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Hub regression failed' }
      - name: Build fresh versioned Windows installer
        run: |
          powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/Build-Installer.ps1 2>&1 | Tee-Object "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/build.log"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Installer build failed' }
      - name: Retrieve published hash-pinned upgrade baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh release download v3.8.2 --repo $env:GITHUB_REPOSITORY --pattern ChatMCPSetup.exe --dir "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-baseline"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Baseline download failed' }
          if ((Get-FileHash "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-baseline/ChatMCPSetup.exe" -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne '75bd3085f73af083d772b675729376d2702448f8a8dc4fe94a9cd58ed80d5564') { throw 'Baseline checksum mismatch' }
      - name: Real setup upgrade, installed EXE lifecycle and uninstall
        run: |
          powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/tests/Test-NativeLifecycle.ps1 -BaselineInstaller "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-baseline/ChatMCPSetup.exe" -CandidateInstaller dist/ChatMCPSetup.exe -OutputDirectory "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/installed-lifecycle"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Installed EXE acceptance failed' }
      - name: Native WebView2 smoke and canonical Companion parity
        run: |
          node CHATMCP-HUB/ui/e2e/webview2-smoke.mjs
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'WebView2 smoke failed' }
          powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/Build-BrowserCompanion.ps1 -VerifyInstallerPayload
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Companion source/ZIP/payload parity failed' }
      - name: Verify final asset checksums and record provenance
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          $assets = @()
          foreach ($name in @('ChatMCPSetup.exe','ChatMCP-Browser-Companion.zip')) {
            $file = Join-Path dist $name
            $actual = (Get-FileHash $file -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
            $expected = ((Get-Content "$file.sha256" -Raw).Trim() -split '\s+')[0].ToLowerInvariant()
            if ($actual -ne $expected) { throw "Checksum mismatch: $name" }
            $assets += [ordered]@{ name=$name; sha256=$actual; bytes=(Get-Item $file).Length }
          }
          $native = Get-Content "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence/installed-lifecycle/report.json" -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
          if ($native.result -ne 'PASS' -or $native.candidateSha256 -ne $assets[0].sha256) { throw 'Native evidence does not match the release EXE' }
          [ordered]@{ version='3.8.3'; companionVersion='1.5.2'; commit=$env:GITHUB_SHA; workflowRun=$env:GITHUB_RUN_ID; assets=$assets; signedInEdgeVerified=$false; authenticodeSigned=$false } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6 | Set-Content dist/RELEASE-MANIFEST.json -Encoding utf8
          python scripts/verify-release-source.py --commit "$env:GITHUB_SHA" --evidence "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/native-release-evidence"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Source or generated-UI payload provenance verification failed' }
      - name: Upload tested release files
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
        with:
          name: ChatMCP-v3.8.3-Windows-and-Companion
          path: |
            dist/ChatMCPSetup.exe
            dist/ChatMCPSetup.exe.sha256
            dist/ChatMCP-Browser-Companion.zip
            dist/ChatMCP-Browser-Companion.zip.sha256
            dist/RELEASE-MANIFEST.json
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Preserve actual Windows evidence even on failure
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
        with:
          name: ChatMCP-v3.8.3-native-evidence
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/native-release-evidence
          if-no-files-found: error
  publish:
    name: Publish verified v3.8.3 release
    needs: [browser, windows]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: read
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      TAG: v3.8.3
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Require regular CI success on this exact release commit
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for attempt in $(seq 1 60); do
            result=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$GITHUB_SHA&event=push&per_page=100" --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.path == ".github/workflows/ci.yml")][0] | [.status // "missing", .conclusion // "none"] | @tsv')
            read -r status conclusion <<< "$result"
            if [ "$status" = completed ]; then
              test "$conclusion" = success || { echo "CI ended: $conclusion"; exit 1; }
              exit 0
            fi
            sleep 15
          done
          echo 'CI did not finish successfully before publication deadline'; exit 1
      - name: Retrieve only artifacts from this successful workflow run
        run: |
          gh run download "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --name ChatMCP-v3.8.3-Windows-and-Companion --dir dist
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib, json, os
          from pathlib import Path
          root = Path('dist')
          manifest = json.loads((root / 'RELEASE-MANIFEST.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig'))
          assert manifest['commit'] == os.environ['GITHUB_SHA']
          assert manifest['version'] == '3.8.3' and manifest['companionVersion'] == '1.5.2'
          assert {a['name'] for a in manifest['assets']} == {'ChatMCPSetup.exe', 'ChatMCP-Browser-Companion.zip'}
          for asset in manifest['assets']:
              file = root / asset['name']
              assert file.stat().st_size == asset['bytes']
              digest = hashlib.file_digest(file.open('rb'), 'sha256').hexdigest()
              assert digest == asset['sha256']
              assert digest == (root / (asset['name'] + '.sha256')).read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig').split()[0]
          print('Exact-commit release asset hashes verified again before publication.')
          PY
      - name: Publish version tag without moving existing tags and release assets
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          test "$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)" = "$GITHUB_SHA" || { echo 'main moved; refusing stale publication'; exit 1; }
          if git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            git fetch origin "refs/tags/$TAG:refs/tags/$TAG"
            test "$(git rev-list -n1 "$TAG")" = "$GITHUB_SHA" || { echo 'Tag points at another commit'; exit 1; }
          else
            git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
            git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
            git tag -a "$TAG" -m 'ChatMCP v3.8.3 - Native Lifecycle and Companion Safety' "$GITHUB_SHA"
            git push origin "refs/tags/$TAG"
          fi
          gh release create "$TAG" dist/ChatMCPSetup.exe dist/ChatMCPSetup.exe.sha256 dist/ChatMCP-Browser-Companion.zip dist/ChatMCP-Browser-Companion.zip.sha256 dist/RELEASE-MANIFEST.json --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --verify-tag --draft --title 'ChatMCP v3.8.3 - Native Lifecycle and Companion Safety' --notes-file RELEASE-NOTES-v3.8.3.md
          gh release edit "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --draft=false --latest
